sentences.zh: 王祥

translations.literal: Wang Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 王祥，字休-{徵}-，琅邪臨沂人，漢諫議大夫吉之-{後}-也。

translations.literal: Wang Xiang, courtesy name Xiuzheng, was a person from Linyi in Langya and a descendant of Han Adviser Grandee Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang, courtesy name Xiuzheng, came from Linyi in Langya—descended from Wang Ji, who had held the post of grand adviser under Han.

sentences.zh: 祖仁，青州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ren was governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang Ren served as governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父融，公府-{辟}-不就。

translations.literal: His father Rong was summoned by the high offices but did not take post.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Rong declined appointments issued by the capital ministries.

sentences.zh: 祥性至孝。

translations.literal: Xiang by nature was utmost filial.
translations.idiomatic: He was exemplary in filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 早喪親，繼母朱氏不慈，數譖之，由是失愛-{於}-父。

translations.literal: Early he lost parents; stepmother the Lady Zhu was not kind; repeatedly slandered him; on this account lost love from father.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he suffered under a stepmother, Lady Zhu, who maligned him until his father turned cold toward him.

sentences.zh: 每使掃除牛下，祥愈恭謹。

translations.literal: Whenever made to sweep beneath the cattle, Xiang became more respectful and careful.
translations.idiomatic: She sent him to muck out the cattle pens; he only grew more diligent and deferential.

sentences.zh: 父母有疾，衣不解帶，湯藥必親嘗。

translations.literal: When father and mother had illness, he did not undo belt from clothes; for decoctions and medicines necessarily personally tasted.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents fell ill he slept in his clothes and tasted every dose before they drank it.

sentences.zh: 母常欲生魚，時天寒冰凍，祥解衣將剖冰求之，冰忽自解，雙鯉躍出，持之而歸。

translations.literal: Mother constantly wished for live fish; at the time Heaven was cold and ice frozen; Xiang removed clothes about to split ice seeking them; ice suddenly of itself released; paired carp leaped out; taking them returned.
translations.idiomatic: She often demanded fresh fish in dead of winter; he stripped and broke the ice to find some—whereupon the ice split open of its own accord and two carp leapt into his hands.

sentences.zh: 母又思黃雀灸，復有黃雀數十飛入其幕，復以供母。

translations.literal: Mother again wished yellow-sparrow roast; again there were several tens of yellow sparrows flying into his curtain; again thereby supplied mother.
translations.idiomatic: When she craved roasted sparrow, dozens flew into his weave-room—and again he brought them to her table.

sentences.zh: 鄕里驚歎，以爲孝感所致焉。

translations.literal: Village and district marveled and sighed, deeming it caused by filial influence.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors declared such wonders could only be Heaven's answer to his devotion.

sentences.zh: 有丹柰結實，母命守之，每風雨，祥輒抱樹而泣。

translations.literal: There was crimson pear bearing fruit; mother ordered guarding it; whenever wind and rain, Xiang always embraced tree and wept.
translations.idiomatic: A red pear tree bore fruit under her orders to guard it; whenever storms threatened the crop he wrapped his arms around the trunk and wept.

sentences.zh: 其篤孝純至如此。

translations.literal: His devoted filial purity reached thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of his filial heart.

sentences.zh: 漢未遭亂，扶母攜弟覽避地廬江，隱居三十餘年，不應州郡之命。

translations.literal: Han end encountered turmoil; supporting mother and leading younger brother Lan, avoided to Lujiang, hid dwelling thirty-odd years, did not respond to province and commandery commands.
translations.idiomatic: As Han collapsed into chaos he led his mother and younger brother Wang Lan to refuge in Lujiang, where they lived in seclusion for more than thirty years and ignored every summons from local authorities.

sentences.zh: 母終，居喪毀瘁，杖而-{後}-起。

translations.literal: Mother ended; dwelling mourning wasted and haggard; with staff thereafter rose.
translations.idiomatic: When she died he mourned until his health broke and could rise only with a staff.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史呂虔檄爲別駕，祥年垂耳順，固辭不受。

translations.literal: Xuzhou Inspector Lu Qian summoned him as aide-de-camp; Xiang's years hung toward ear-compliance; firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qian, inspector of Xuzhou, appointed him aide-de-camp, but though nearly sixty Wang Xiang firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 覽勸之，爲具車牛，祥乃應召，虔委以州事。

translations.literal: Lan exhorted him; for him prepared cart and ox; Xiang then answered summons; Qian entrusted him with provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lan persuaded him and furnished cart and oxen; Wang Xiang then took office, and Lu Qian handed him the administration.

sentences.zh: -{於}-時寇盜充斥，祥率勵兵士，頻討破之。

translations.literal: At that time bandits and robbers filled everywhere; Xiang led and encouraged soldiers; repeatedly attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits swarmed the region; he rallied the troops and repeatedly routed them.

sentences.zh: 州界清靜，政化大行。

translations.literal: The province's borders clear and quiet; governance transformation greatly proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit grew peaceful and his policies took full effect.

sentences.zh: 時人歌之曰：「海沂之康，實賴王祥。

translations.literal: People of the time sang of him saying: 'The Hai-Yi region's peace truly relies on Wang Xiang.'
translations.idiomatic: Folk sang: "Peace along the coast owes everything to Wang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 邦國不空，別駕之功。」

translations.literal: 'The state is not empty—the aide-de-camp's achievement.'
translations.idiomatic: The treasury stays full—credit the aide-de-camp.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，除溫令，累遷大司農。

translations.literal: Recommended cultivated talent; appointed Wen county magistrate; accumulated promotions to Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a cultivated talent, he became magistrate of Wen and rose eventually to Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄕公即位，與定策功，封關內侯，拜光祿勳，轉司隸校尉。

translations.literal: When Duke of Gaoguixiang ascended the throne, for participating in settling-the-policy merit, enfeoffed estate-inside marquis, appointed Supervisor of the Household, transferred Metropolitan Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Mao took the throne Wang Xiang shared credit for the coup and received a marquisate within the passes, then posts as Supervisor of the Household and metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 從討毌丘儉，增邑四百戸，遷太常，封萬歲亭侯。

translations.literal: Following in attacking Guanqiu Jian; increased fief four hundred households; promoted Minister of Ceremonies; enfeoffed Marquis of Wansui village.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against Guanqiu Jian, gained four hundred extra households, became Minister of Ceremonies, and was titled marquis of Wansui village.

sentences.zh: 天子幸太學，命祥爲三老。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven visited the Imperial Academy; ordered Xiang as one of the Three Elders.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the academy he named Wang Xiang one of the three elders.

sentences.zh: 祥南面几杖，以師道自居。

translations.literal: Xiang faced south with bench and staff; by teacher's way placed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He faced south with armrest and staff, acting as imperial mentor.

sentences.zh: 天子北面乞言，祥陳明王聖帝君臣政化之要以訓之，聞者莫不砥礪。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven faced north begging words; Xiang displayed enlightened kings and sage emperors, lord and minister governance transformation's essentials thereby to instruct them; hearers none did not hone themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned north to seek counsel; Wang Xiang laid out how sage rulers and ministers ordered the realm, and every listener resolved to better himself.

sentences.zh: 及高貴鄕公之弑也，朝臣舉哀，祥號哭曰「老臣無狀」，涕淚交流，眾有愧色。

translations.literal: When Duke of Gaoguixiang's assassination occurred, court ministers raised mourning; Xiang wailed crying saying 'Old minister without shape'; tears and mucus interflowed; crowd had ashamed expression.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Mao's murder the court went into mourning; Wang Xiang sobbed that he had failed his sovereign, tears streaming until others flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 頃之，拜司空，轉太尉，加侍中。

translations.literal: Shortly, appointed Minister of Works; transferred Grand Commandant; added palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Minister of Works, then Grand Commandant with concurrent palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 五等建，封睢陵侯，邑一千六百戸。

translations.literal: Five ranks established; enfeoffed Marquis of Suiling; fief one thousand six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the five noble ranks were instituted he became Marquis of Suiling with sixteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及武帝爲晉王，祥與荀顗往謁，顗謂祥曰：「相王尊重，何侯既已盡敬，今便當拜也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu became Prince of Jin, Xiang with Xun Yi went to visit; Yi said to Xiang: 'The minister-king is honored and weighty; Marquis He already has exhausted respect—now ought to bow.'
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan was Prince of Jin, Wang Xiang visited with Xun Yi, who urged him: "The prince ranks supreme—He Zeng has already bowed; we must follow suit.

sentences.zh: 」祥曰：「相國誠爲尊貴，然是魏之宰相。

translations.literal: ' Xiang said: 'The minister truly is honored and noble—yet he is Wei's minister.'
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xiang replied: "He may be exalted, but he remains Wei’s chief minister.

sentences.zh: 吾等魏之三公，公王相去，一階而已，班例大同，安有天子三司而輒拜人者！

translations.literal: We are Wei's three dukes; duke and king separated by only one rank; court precedent greatly same—how can there be Heaven's son three ministers who casually bow to others!
translations.idiomatic: We three dukes of Wei stand one rank below a king—protocol barely differs—how could ministers of the Wei court bow casually to anyone?

sentences.zh: 損魏朝之望，虧晉王之德，君子愛人以禮，吾不爲也。

translations.literal: Diminishing Wei court's prestige; harming Jin prince's virtue—a gentleman loves others by ritual; I do not do it.'
translations.idiomatic: It would shame Wei and tarnish the prince's virtue; the gentleman treats others with ritual propriety—I will not bow.

sentences.zh: 」及入，顗遂拜，而祥獨長揖。

translations.literal: ' When they entered, Yi then bowed; but Xiang alone extended deep bow.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the hall Xun Yi kowtowed while Wang Xiang merely bowed at the waist.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「今日方知君見顧之重矣！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'Today I then know lord's regard shown weighty!'
translations.idiomatic: The prince exclaimed, "Now I see how highly you esteem yourself!"

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，拜太保，進爵爲公，加置七官之職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne; appointed Grand Guardian; advanced noble rank to duke; added establishment of seven offices' duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan became emperor he made Wang Xiang grand guardian, raised him to duke, and enlarged his staff.

sentences.zh: 帝新愛命，虛己以求讜言。

translations.literal: The Emperor newly received mandate; emptied self to seek forthright words.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh to the mandate, the emperor humbled himself for blunt counsel.

sentences.zh: 祥與何曾、鄭-{沖}-等耆艾篤老，希復朝見，帝遣侍中任愷諮問得失，及政化所先。

translations.literal: Xiang with He Zeng, Zheng Chong and others aged hoary deeply old; rarely again court audience; Emperor dispatched palace attendant Ren Kai to consult on gain and loss, and governance transformation's priorities.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang, He Zeng, Zheng Chong, and other aged ministers seldom attended court, so the emperor sent Ren Kai to ask their judgment on policy priorities.

sentences.zh: 祥以年老疲耄，累乞遜位，帝不許。

translations.literal: Xiang because old age weary and aged; repeatedly begged yielding position; Emperor did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang pleaded age and exhaustion and repeatedly asked to retire; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞侯史光以祥久疾，闕朝會禮，請免祥官。

translations.literal: Attendant Secretary Imperial Counsellor Hou Shiguang because Xiang long ill; lacked court assembly ritual; requested dismiss Xiang's office.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Counsellor Hou Shiguang impeached him for chronic illness and absence from court, seeking his removal.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「太保元老高行，朕所毗倚以隆政道者也。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'The Grand Guardian is elder pillar with lofty conduct—what We rely on to enlarge governance's way.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict answered: "The grand guardian is a pillar of virtue on whom I rely to elevate government.

sentences.zh: 前-{後}-遜讓，不從所執，此非有司所得議也。

translations.literal: Former and latter yielding decline; not following what he held—this is not what responsible officials may deliberate.'
translations.idiomatic: His repeated resignations were declined—this is no matter for petty officials to debate.

sentences.zh: 」遂寢光奏。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon shelved Guang's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Shiguang's memorial was tabled.

sentences.zh: 祥固乞骸骨，詔聽以睢陵公就第，位同保傅，在三司之右，祿賜如前。

translations.literal: Xiang firmly begged bones; edict permitted him as Duke of Suiling to go to mansion; rank same as guardian-tutors; to right of three ministers; salary and gifts as before.
translations.idiomatic: When he insisted on retiring, the emperor let him withdraw as Duke of Suiling with honors rivalling the tutors', precedence above the three ministers, and stipends unchanged.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「古之致仕，不事王侯。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Ancient retiring from office did not serve kings and marquises.'
translations.idiomatic: The edict noted: "Ancient retirees owed no duty to local lords.

sentences.zh: 今雖以國公留居京邑，不宜復苦以朝請。

translations.literal: Now although by state duke retained dwelling capital city; not fitting again to distress with court attendance requests.'
translations.idiomatic: Though you remain in the capital as a duke of state, you need not weary yourself with dawn audiences.

sentences.zh: 其賜几杖，不朝，大事皆諮訪之。

translations.literal: Gift him bench and staff; no court; great affairs all consult and visit him.'
translations.idiomatic: Grant him armrest and staff, exempt him from court, yet consult him on every weighty affair.

sentences.zh: 賜安車駟馬，第一區，錢百萬，絹五百匹，床帳簟褥，以舍人六人爲睢陵公舍人，置官騎二十人。

translations.literal: Gift peaceful carriage four-horses; first-grade compound; cash million; silk five hundred bolts; bed curtains reed mats cushions; using six chamberlains as Duke of Suiling's chamberlains; establish official riders twenty men.'
translations.idiomatic: Award him a carriage and team, a top-ranked mansion, a million cash, five hundred bolts of silk, bedding and mats, six household stewards, and twenty mounted guards.

sentences.zh: 以公子騎都尉肇爲給事中，使常優遊定省。

translations.literal: Using noble son Cavalry Commandant Zhao as palace secretary; cause constantly leisurely comfort and visit.'
translations.idiomatic: Appoint his son Wang Zhao, cavalry commandant, as palace secretary so he may tend his father at ease.

sentences.zh: 又乙太保高潔清素，家無宅宇，其權留本府，須所賜第成乃出。」

translations.literal: Further yi: Grand Guardian lofty pure clear plain; house without mansion buildings; temporarily retain original office; wait until gifted mansion completed then emerge.'
translations.idiomatic: It was further stated: "The grand guardian lives plainly and owns no house—let him lodge meanwhile in his old ministry until the granted mansion is finished."

sentences.zh: 及疾篤，著遺令訓子孫曰：「夫生之有死，自然之理。

translations.literal: When illness severe; composed testament instructing sons and grandsons saying: 'Now birth having death is nature's pattern.'
translations.idiomatic: Near death he wrote instructions for his heirs: "Life ends in death—that is nature's law.

sentences.zh: 吾年八十有五，啟手何恨。

translations.literal: My years eighty-five; clean hands—what regret?
translations.idiomatic: I am eighty-five and may lay down my tasks without regret.

sentences.zh: 不有遺言，使爾無述。

translations.literal: Without testament words; causing you nothing to narrate.'
translations.idiomatic: Without a few last words you would have nothing to recall of me.

sentences.zh: 吾生值季末，登庸曆試，無毗佐之勳，沒無以報。

translations.literal: My life encountered season's end; ascended employment passed trials; without assisting merit; dying nothing wherewith to repay.'
translations.idiomatic: I lived in a declining age, served when summoned, and never earned merit worth mentioning—I leave nothing to repay the state.

sentences.zh: 氣絶但洗手足，不須沐浴，勿纏屍，皆浣故衣，隨時所服。

translations.literal: When breath cuts only wash hands and feet; not need bathe; do not wrap corpse; all wash old clothes; according to season what was worn.'
translations.idiomatic: When I die wash only hands and feet—no full bath, no winding-sheet—dress me in laundered clothes I actually wore.

sentences.zh: 所賜山玄玉佩、衞氏玉玦、綬笥皆勿以斂。

translations.literal: Gifted mountain-dark jade pendant, Wei clan jade pendant-girdle, ribbon box—all do not use for encoffining.'
translations.idiomatic: Do not bury the dark jade pendant, Wei-clan ring, or ribbon case the court gave me.

sentences.zh: 西芒上土自堅貞，勿用甓石，勿起墳隴。

translations.literal: Western Mang upland soil naturally firm chaste; do not use brick stone; do not raise mound ridge.'
translations.idiomatic: The loess on Mount Mang is firm enough—no brick facing, no raised tumulus.

sentences.zh: 穿深二丈，槨取容棺。

translations.literal: Dig depth two zhang; outer coffin takes capacity inner coffin.'
translations.idiomatic: Dig two zhang deep and let the outer shell barely fit the inner coffin.

sentences.zh: 勿作前堂、布几筵、置書箱鏡奩之具，棺前但可施床榻而已。

translations.literal: Do not make front hall; spread bench mats; place book chest mirror box tools; before coffin only may apply bed couch only.'
translations.idiomatic: No memorial hall, no arranged vessels, no books or mirrors—only a couch before the coffin.

sentences.zh: Я脯各一盤，玄酒一杯，爲朝夕奠。

translations.literal: Dried jujubes and sliced meats, one plate each; dark wine one cup; for morning and evening offerings.'
translations.idiomatic: Place dried jujubes and cured meats on separate plates with a cup of unstrained wine for the dawn and dusk oblations.

sentences.zh: 家人大小不須送喪，大小祥乃設特牲。

translations.literal: Family great and small not need escort mourning; great and small auspicious then set special beast.'
translations.idiomatic: Kin need not join the funeral train; reserve a single beast offering for the first- and second-year memorials.

sentences.zh: 無違餘命！

translations.literal: Do not disobey remaining commands!
translations.idiomatic: Do not disobey these orders!

sentences.zh: 高柴泣血三年，夫子謂之愚。

translations.literal: Gao Chai wept blood three years; the Master called it foolish.'
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chai wept blood for three years—Confucius called that folly.

sentences.zh: 閔子除喪出見。

translations.literal: Minzi removed mourning went out to see.'
translations.idiomatic: When Min Sun ended mourning and appeared in public again

sentences.zh: 援琴切切而哀，仲尼謂之孝。

translations.literal: grasped zither anxious and grief; Zhongni called it filial.'
translations.idiomatic: he took up his lute in poignant grief—Confucius named that true filial piety.

sentences.zh: 故哭泣之哀，日月降殺，飲食之宜，自有-{制}-度。

translations.literal: Therefore weeping's grief; sun and moon descend degrees; drinking and eating's appropriateness; naturally has regulation measure.'
translations.idiomatic: Thus mourning weakens by prescribed months, and food follows measured ritual rules.

sentences.zh: 夫言行可覆，信之至也；

translations.literal: Now speech and action can be reviewed—trust's utmost;
translations.idiomatic: Speech and deeds that withstand scrutiny show utmost good faith;

sentences.zh: 推美引過，德之至也；

translations.literal: pushing beauty drawing fault—virtue's utmost;
translations.idiomatic: Giving credit to others while owning one's faults shows utmost virtue;

sentences.zh: 揚名顯親，孝之至也；

translations.literal: raising name displaying kin—filial piety's utmost;
translations.idiomatic: Raising one's parents' renown fulfills the highest filial duty;

sentences.zh: 兄弟怡怡，宗族欣欣，悌之至也；

translations.literal: brothers harmonious; lineage joyful—fraternal submission's utmost;
translations.idiomatic: harmony among brothers and cheer in the clan fulfill fraternal duty;

sentences.zh: 臨財莫過乎讓：此五者，立身之本。

translations.literal: facing wealth none surpasses yielding: these five are establishing body's roots.'
translations.idiomatic: facing gain, yield—those five are the foundation of character.

sentences.zh: 顏子所以爲命，未之思也，夫何遠之有！

translations.literal: What Yanzi took as life's mandate—if not pondered it, how far is there!
translations.idiomatic: They were Yan Hui's lifework—reflect on them and they are never beyond reach!

sentences.zh: 」其子皆奉而行之。

translations.literal: ' His sons all upheld and practiced them.
translations.idiomatic: His sons obeyed every clause.

sentences.zh: 薨，詔賜東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，錢三十萬，布帛百匹。

translations.literal: Died; edict gifted Eastern Park secret vessels; court robes one set; clothes one suit; cash three hundred thousand; cloth silk hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the court supplied burial gear from the imperial workshop, a court robe, a suit, three hundred thousand cash, and a hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 時文明皇太后崩始逾月，其-{後}-詔曰：「爲睢陵公發哀，事乃至今。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Dowager Wenming's death had just passed a month; afterward edict said: 'For Duke of Suiling raising mourning, affair reaches till now.'
translations.idiomatic: Only a month had passed since Empress Dowager Wenming died when another edict noted: "We have yet to mourn the Duke of Suiling properly.

sentences.zh: 雖每爲之感傷，要未得特敘哀情。

translations.literal: Although constantly for this felt wounded sorrow; essential not yet obtained specially narrating grief feeling.'
translations.idiomatic: Though each death pains me, his loss still lacks its own observance.

sentences.zh: 今便哭之。

translations.literal: Now then weep him.'
translations.idiomatic: Let me weep for him now.

sentences.zh: 」明年，策諡曰元。

translations.literal: ' Next year, patent posthumous name said Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received the posthumous title Yuan.

sentences.zh: 祥之薨，奔赴者非朝廷之賢，則親親故吏而已，門無雜吊之賓。

translations.literal: At Xiang's death, those rushing to attend were not court's worthies, then kin and old clerks only; gate without miscellaneous condolence guests.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hurried to his funeral were court worthies or old friends and former staff alone—no casual mourners clogged his gate.

sentences.zh: 族孫戎歎曰：「太保可謂清達矣！

translations.literal: Lineage grandson Rong sighed saying: 'The Grand Guardian can be called pure and penetrating!'
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Wang Rong sighed, "The grand guardian died as plainly as he lived!"

sentences.zh: 」又稱：「祥在正始，不在能言之流。

translations.literal: ' Again praised: 'Xiang at Zhengshi era was not among eloquent-speech cohort.'
translations.idiomatic: He added: "In the Zhengshi years Wang Xiang never counted among the clever talkers.

sentences.zh: 及與之言，理致清遠，將非以德掩其言乎！

translations.literal: When with him spoke; principle reached clear far—perhaps not by virtue covering his speech!
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever he spoke, his reasoning ran lucid and deep—perhaps virtue simply silenced idle words!

sentences.zh: 」祥有五子：肇、夏、馥、烈、芬。

translations.literal: ' Xiang had five sons: Zhao, Xia, Fu, Lie, Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang had five sons: Zhao, Xia, Fu, Lie, and Fen.

sentences.zh: 肇孽庶，夏早卒，馥嗣爵。

translations.literal: Zhao was bastard-child of concubine; Xia early died; Fu succeeded noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was born to a concubine; Xia died young; Fu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，以祥家甚貧儉，賜絹三百匹，拜馥上洛太守，卒諡曰孝。

translations.literal: Xianning beginning; because Xiang household very poor frugal; gifted silk three hundred bolts; appointed Fu Shangluo governor; died posthumous name said Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning the court granted three hundred bolts of silk because the family remained poor, appointed Fu governor of Shangluo, and posthumously titled him Xiao.

sentences.zh: 子根嗣，散騎郎。

translations.literal: Son Gen succeeded; supernumerary cavalier gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Gen succeeded him as a supernumerary gentleman-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 肇仕至始平太守。

translations.literal: Zhao served reaching Shiping governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao rose to governor of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 肇子俊，守太子舍人，封永世侯。

translations.literal: Zhao's son Jun; acting crown prince household aide; enfeoffed Marquis of Yongshi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's son Jun served as acting household aide to the heir and was titled marquis of Yongshi.

sentences.zh: 俊子遐，郁林太守。

translations.literal: Jun's son Xia; Yulin governor.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's son Xia became governor of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 烈、芬並幼知名，爲祥所愛。

translations.literal: Lie and Fen both in youth known by name; by Xiang loved.
translations.idiomatic: Lie and Fen were prodigies whom Wang Xiang adored.

sentences.zh: 二子亦同時而亡。

translations.literal: Two sons likewise same time died.
translations.idiomatic: Both died on the same day.

sentences.zh: 將死，烈欲還葬舊土，芬欲留葬京邑。

translations.literal: About to die; Lie wished return burial old soil; Fen wished retain burial capital city.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, Lie wished to lie in their homeland while Fen preferred the capital.

sentences.zh: 祥流涕曰：「不忘故鄕，仁也；

translations.literal: Xiang flowing tears said: 'Not forgetting old village—benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang wept: "Longing for home is humanity;

sentences.zh: 不戀本土，達也。

translations.literal: not clinging native soil—penetrating.'
translations.idiomatic: refusing to cling to native soil is enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 惟仁與達，吾二子有焉。」

translations.literal: Only benevolence and penetrating—my two sons have them.'
translations.idiomatic: Each of my sons possessed one of those virtues.

translations.literal: The digit edition inserts an equals sign as a layout divider.
translations.idiomatic: Here the digitized text marks a column break with an equals sign.

sentences.zh: 祥弟 覽

translations.literal: Xiang's younger brother Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lan, younger brother of Wang Xiang.

translations.literal: Equals sign serving as edition divider.
translations.idiomatic: Another equals-sign divider precedes the subsection proper.

sentences.zh: 覽字玄通。

translations.literal: Lan's courtesy name Xuantong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lan's courtesy name was Xuantong.

sentences.zh: 母朱，遇祥無道。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Zhu, treated Wang Xiang with cruelty and refused him proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother, Lady Zhu, was vicious toward Wang Xiang and denied him ordinary decency.

sentences.zh: 覽年數歲，見祥被楚撻，輒涕泣抱持。

translations.literal: When Wang Lan was only a few years old, whenever he saw Xiang beaten with the rod, he would weep and cling to him.
translations.idiomatic: While Lan was still a small child, each time he witnessed Xiang flogged he burst into tears and held him fast.

sentences.zh: 至-{於}-成童，每諫其母，其母少止凶虐。

translations.literal: When he reached the age of capped youth, he often remonstrated with his mother, and she somewhat checked her violent cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he came of age he repeatedly pleaded with his mother, who then moderated her harsh abuse.

sentences.zh: 朱屢以非理使祥，覽輒與祥俱。

translations.literal: Lady Zhu repeatedly assigned Xiang unreasonable tasks, and Lan always went with Xiang to do them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhu forced Xiang into unjust errands, Lan insisted on sharing the labor.

sentences.zh: 又虐使祥妻，覽妻亦趨而共之。

translations.literal: She also cruelly imposed labors on Xiang's wife; Lan's wife likewise hurried to join in doing them.
translations.idiomatic: She maltreated Xiang's wife as well, and Lan's wife rushed to take part so the burden would not fall on her alone.

sentences.zh: 朱患之，乃止。

translations.literal: Lady Zhu worried over this and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, troubled by their solidarity, gave up the practice.

sentences.zh: 祥喪父之-{後}-，漸有時譽。

translations.literal: After Xiang lost his father, he gradually gained a timely reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiang's father had died, his reputation slowly began to rise.

sentences.zh: 朱深疾之，密使鴆祥。

translations.literal: Lady Zhu deeply hated him and secretly ordered Xiang poisoned with zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu nursed a bitter grudge and secretly tried to kill him with poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 覽知之，徑起取酒。

translations.literal: Lan learned of it and straightway rose and took the wine.
translations.idiomatic: Lan found out, stood up at once, and seized the cup.

sentences.zh: 祥疑其有毒，爭而不與，朱遽奪反之。

translations.literal: Xiang suspected it was poisoned, struggled and would not yield it; Zhu suddenly snatched it back.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang feared it was tainted and refused to let go; Zhu tore the cup away in haste.

sentences.zh: 自-{後}-朱賜祥饌，覽輒先嘗。

translations.literal: After that, whenever Zhu gave Xiang food, Lan always tasted it first.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever Zhu sent Xiang a meal, Lan sampled it before Xiang ate.

sentences.zh: 朱懼覽致斃，遂止。

translations.literal: Zhu feared Lan might die from it and therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid Lan would die from tasting it, she abandoned the scheme.

sentences.zh: 覽孝友恭恪，名亞-{於}-祥。

translations.literal: Lan was filial, fraternal, respectful, and conscientious; his fame ranked second to Xiang's.
translations.idiomatic: Lan showed filial piety, brotherly devotion, and punctilious respect; only Xiang's name stood above his.

sentences.zh: 及祥仕進，覽亦應本郡之召，稍遷司徒西曹掾、清河太守。

translations.literal: When Xiang entered official service, Lan also answered a summons from his home commandery, and was gradually promoted to Western Bureau Clerk under the Minister of Education and Prefect of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiang advanced in office, Lan took up a local appointment too, rising step by step to Western Bureau Clerk of the Minister of Education and then prefect of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 五等建，封即丘子，邑六百戸。

translations.literal: When the five noble ranks were instituted, he was enfeoffed Baron of Jiqiu with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Under the new five-rank system he received the barony of Jiqiu with six hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 泰始末，除弘訓少府。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taishi reign he was appointed Junior Mentor of the Hongxun household.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taishi he became Junior Mentor of the Hongxun establishment.

sentences.zh: 職省，轉太中大夫，祿賜與卿同。

translations.literal: The office was abolished; he was transferred to Grand Counselor, with salary and gifts equal to those of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: When that post was cut, he moved to Grand Counselor on stipends and largesse matching a senior minister.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，詔曰：「覽少篤至行，服仁履義，貞素之操，長而彌固。

translations.literal: Early in the Xianning era an edict stated that in youth Lan practiced the utmost in conduct; he embraced benevolence and trod in righteousness; his chaste and plain integrity grew ever firmer with age.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xianning the throne proclaimed that Lan had shown singular virtue from boyhood, grounding himself in humanity and right, and that his simplicity only deepened over the years.

sentences.zh: 其以覽爲宗正卿。

translations.literal: Let Wang Lan be appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: The edict named him Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，以疾上疏乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, citing illness, he submitted a memorial begging leave to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, pleading sickness, he asked permission to resign and return home.

sentences.zh: 詔聽之，乙太中大夫歸老，賜錢二十萬，床帳薦褥，遣殿中醫療疾給藥。

translations.literal: The edict granted his request; he retired as Grand Counselor to old age; he was given two hundred thousand cash, bed curtains, mats, and bedding; palace physicians were dispatched to treat his illness and supply medicine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved; he went home with the rank of Grand Counselor, received two hundred thousand coins, bedding and furnishings, and court physicians with medicines were sent to attend him.

sentences.zh: -{後}-轉光祿大夫，門施行馬。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Household Counselor, with horse-blocks placed before his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently raised to Household Counselor and granted the privilege of mounting-blocks at his doorway.

sentences.zh: 卒，時年七十三，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-three; his posthumous title was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-three and was canonized as Zhen.

sentences.zh: 有六子：裁、基、會、正、彥、琛。

translations.literal: He had six sons: Cai, Ji, Hui, Zheng, Yan, and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His six sons were Cai, Ji, Hui, Zheng, Yan, and Chen.

sentences.zh: 裁字士初，撫軍長史。

translations.literal: Cai, courtesy Shichu, was Chief Clerk to the Army that Pacifies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cai, styled Shichu, served as chief clerk on the staff of the Army that Pacifies.

sentences.zh: 基字士先，治書御史。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy Shixian, was Secretary Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, styled Shixian, held the post of secretary censor.

sentences.zh: 會字士和，侍御史。

translations.literal: Hui, courtesy Shihe, was Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, styled Shihe, was an attending censor.

sentences.zh: 正字士則，尚書郎。

translations.literal: Zheng, courtesy Shize, was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zheng, styled Shize, served as a gentleman at the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 彥字士治，中護軍。

translations.literal: Yan, courtesy Shizhi, was Central Army Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, styled Shizhi, became central army protector.

sentences.zh: 琛字士瑋，國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Chen, courtesy Shiwei, was Libationer of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen, styled Shiwei, rose to libationer of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 初，呂虔有佩刀，工相之，以爲必登三公，可服此刀。

translations.literal: Long before, Lü Qian had possessed an inscribed saber; craftsmen had divined over it and concluded that only one who would surely attain one of the Three Dukes could properly wear this blade.
translations.idiomatic: In an earlier day Lü Qian owned a ceremonial sword whose craftsmen prophesied that only a future holder of one of the Three Dukes' seats was fit to bear it.

sentences.zh: 虔謂祥曰：「苟非其人，刀或爲害。

translations.literal: Qian said to Xiang: If it is not the right man, the saber may bring harm.
translations.idiomatic: Qian warned Xiang that in the wrong hands the blade might bring disaster.

sentences.zh: 卿有公輔之量，故以相與。

translations.literal: You have the capacity of a minister of state; therefore I give it to you.
translations.idiomatic: You have the stature of a chief minister, so I entrust the sword to you.

sentences.zh: 」祥固辭，強之乃受。

translations.literal: Xiang firmly declined; when pressed he accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang refused repeatedly but yielded when Qian insisted.

sentences.zh: 祥臨薨，以刀授覽，曰：「汝-{後}-必興，足稱此刀。

translations.literal: On the verge of death Xiang handed the saber to Lan and said: Your descendants will surely flourish and will be worthy of this blade.
translations.idiomatic: As death approached Xiang passed the sword to Lan, telling him that his line would rise and prove worthy of the heirloom.

sentences.zh: 」覽-{後}-奕世多賢才，興-{於}-江左矣。

translations.literal: Lan's descendants for generations produced many worthy talents and rose to prominence south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Lan's posterity for generations yielded distinguished men who made their mark in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 裁子導，別有傳。

translations.literal: Cai's son Dao has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Cai's son Dao is treated in another chapter.

sentences.zh: 鄭沖

translations.literal: Zheng Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zheng Chong.

sentences.zh: 鄭-{沖}-，字文和，滎陽開封人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Chong, courtesy Wenhe, was a native of Kaifeng in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chong, whose courtesy name was Wenhe, came from Kaifeng in the Xingyang region.

sentences.zh: 起自寒微，卓爾立操，清恬寡欲，耽玩經史，遂博究儒術及百家之言。

translations.literal: He rose from humble origins, stood apart in establishing his conduct, was clear-minded, quiet, and had few desires; he immersed himself in the classics and histories and thus broadly mastered Confucian teaching and the writings of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Of low birth yet strikingly principled, he lived plainly with little appetite for gain, devoured classical texts, and gained wide learning in Confucian doctrine and other schools.

sentences.zh: 有姿望，動必循禮，任真自守，不要鄕曲之譽，由是州郡久不加禮。

translations.literal: He had bearing and reputation; in movement he always followed ritual; he kept to his true nature and did not court praise in his village; for this reason commanderies long declined to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: He carried himself with dignity and obeyed ritual in every act, shunning local fame; county authorities therefore neglected him for years.

sentences.zh: 及魏文帝爲太子，搜揚側陋，命-{沖}-爲文學，累遷尚書郎，出補陳留太守。

translations.literal: When the Wei Emperor Wen was heir apparent, he sought talent in obscure places and appointed Chong Literary Scholar; Chong was repeatedly promoted to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and then went out as Administrator of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Wendi was crown prince he recruited hidden talent and named Chong literary attendant; Chong climbed to gentleman at the Masters of Writing and later became administrator of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: -{沖}-以儒雅爲德，蒞職無幹局之譽，簞食縕袍，不營資產，世以此重之。

translations.literal: Chong took scholarly refinement as his virtue; in office he won no reputation for administrative grasp; he ate from a bamboo basket and wore patched robes and did not accumulate property; the age therefore esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: He modeled himself on classical virtue rather than bureaucratic flair, lived frugally, and built no fortune, which won deep respect.

sentences.zh: 大將軍曹爽引爲從事中郎，轉散騎常侍、光祿勳。

translations.literal: General-in-chief Cao Shuang brought him in as Attendant Clerk; he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Household Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang enlisted him as attendant clerk; he moved on to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and household counselor.

sentences.zh: ，拜司空。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 及高貴鄕公講《尚書》，-{沖}-執經親授，與侍中鄭小同俱被賞賜。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang lectured on the Documents, Chong held the classic and instructed him personally; together with Palace Attendant Zheng Xiaotong he received imperial gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Duke Gaoguixiang's seminar on the Documents, Chong lectured from the text beside Zheng Xiaotong, and both were rewarded.

sentences.zh: 俄轉司徒。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was shortly shifted to minister of education.

sentences.zh: 常道鄕公即位，拜太保，位在三司之上，封壽光侯。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Changdaoxiang ascended the throne, Chong was appointed Grand Tutor, ranked above the Three Dukes, and enfeoffed Marquis of Shouguang.
translations.idiomatic: At Changdaoxiang's accession Chong became grand tutor, senior to the three highest ministers, with the marquisate of Shouguang.

sentences.zh: -{沖}-雖位階台輔，而不預世事。

translations.literal: Though Chong stood among the terrace ministers, he did not involve himself in current politics.
translations.idiomatic: Despite sitting among the highest counselors he stayed clear of factional business.

sentences.zh: 時文帝輔政，平蜀之-{後}-，命賈充、羊祜等分定禮儀、律令，皆先諮-{於}--{沖}-，然-{後}-施行。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assisted in government, after Shu had been pacified he ordered Jia Chong, Yang Hu, and others to divide the drafting of ritual and statutes; all first consulted Chong and only afterward put measures into effect.
translations.idiomatic: During Wendi's regency, once Shu fell, Jia Chong and Yang Hu were tasked with codifying ritual and law only after Chong had been consulted on each step.

sentences.zh: 及魏帝告禪，使-{沖}-奉策。

translations.literal: When the Wei emperor announced abdication to Jin, Chong was sent to present the patent of succession.
translations.idiomatic: At the Wei abdication Chong carried the formal patent transferring the mandate.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，拜太傅，進爵爲公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Chong was appointed Grand Instructor and his noble rank was raised to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi named him grand instructor and elevated his fief to duke.

sentences.zh: 頃之，司隸李憙、中丞侯史光奏-{沖}-及何曾，荀顗等各以疾病，俱應免官。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Metropolitan Commandant Li Xi and Palace Assistant Censor Hou Shiguang memorialized that Chong, He Zeng, Xun Yi, and others, each citing illness, ought all to be dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Xi and Hou Shiguang urged that Chong, He Zeng, Xun Yi, and others retire on grounds of sickness.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne refused.

sentences.zh: -{沖}-遂不視事，表乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Chong then ceased to attend to duties and memorialized begging to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Chong stopped reporting for duty and asked to yield his post.

sentences.zh: 優詔不許，遣使申喻。

translations.literal: A gracious edict refused; an envoy was sent to explain.
translations.idiomatic: An indulgent rescript denied him and an envoy reasoned with him.

sentences.zh: -{沖}-固辭，上貂蟬印綬，詔又不許。

translations.literal: Chong firmly declined and submitted his gold-cicada seals and ribbons; the edict again refused.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed his resignation and returned his insignia; again the court declined.

sentences.zh: ，詔曰：「昔漢祖以知人善任，克平宇宙，推述勳勞，歸美三俊。

translations.literal: An edict stated that formerly Han Gaozu, by knowing good men and employing them well, was able to pacify the realm; he attributed merit and credited the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: A decree recalled how Han Gaozu matched talent to office, unified the empire, and praised his chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 遂與功臣剖符作誓，藏之宗廟，副在有司，所以明德庸勳，籓翼王室者也。

translations.literal: He then with his merit subjects split tallies and swore oaths, stored them in the ancestral temple and kept copies with the authorities, thereby clarifying virtue and rewarding merit and fencing and aiding the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: They split tallies, lodged oaths in the ancestral shrine, and filed duplicates with the ministries to honor service and shield the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 昔我祖考，遭世多難，攬授英俊，與之斷金，遂濟時務，克定大業。

translations.literal: Formerly our ancestors met an age of many hardships; they gathered worthy men and with them swore an alliance firm as metal; thus they aided the times and settled the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Our forebears in turbulent times rallied able allies in bonds strong as metal and so laid the foundation of the realm.

sentences.zh: 太傅壽光公鄭-{沖}-、太保郎陵公何曾、太尉臨淮公荀顗各尚德依仁，明允篤誠，翼亮先皇，光濟帝業。

translations.literal: Grand Instructor Duke of Shouguang Zheng Chong, Grand Tutor Duke of Langling He Zeng, and Grand Commandant Duke of Linhuai Xun Yi each esteemed virtue and relied on benevolence; they were perspicuous, trustworthy, and sincere; they aided and illumined the former emperor and enlarged the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, He Zeng, and Xun Yi—the dukes of Shouguang, Langling, and Linhuai—were paragons of virtue who steadied the late emperor and enlarged his achievement.

sentences.zh: 故司空博陵元公王沈、衞將軍钜平侯羊祜才兼文武，忠肅居正，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The late Minister of Works Yuan Duke of Boling Wang Shen and Guards General Marquis of Juping Yang Hu combined civil and military talent; they were loyal, solemn, and upright; We greatly commend them.
translations.idiomatic: The departed Wang Shen of Boling and Yang Hu of Juping united civil and military gifts with steadfast loyalty, which We heartily applaud.

sentences.zh: 《書》不云乎：'天秩有禮，五服五章哉！

translations.literal: Does not the Documents say: 'Heaven orders ranks by ritual; the five garments have five patterns!'
translations.idiomatic: As the Documents asks, has not Heaven ordained hierarchy through ritual and the five grades of dress?

sentences.zh: '其爲壽光、郎陵、臨淮、博陵、钜平國置郎中令，假夫人、世子印綬，食本秩三分之一，皆如郡公侯比。」

translations.literal: They shall establish for the states of Shouguang, Langling, Linhuai, Boling, and Juping each a palace steward; lend seals to wives and heirs; grant salary at one-third of the original rank; all shall be treated like commandery dukes and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Palace stewards were ordered for those five princedoms, consorts and heirs received borrowed seals, stipends ran at one-third of former rank, all on the model of commandery-level peers.

sentences.zh: 九年，-{沖}-又抗表致仕。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Chong again submitted a memorial insisting on retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine Chong renewed his plea to retire.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「太傅韞德深粹，履行高潔，恬遠清虛，確然絶世。

translations.literal: The edict stated that the Grand Instructor embodies virtue deep and pure; his conduct is lofty and clean; he is tranquil, remote, clear, and empty; he stands decisively apart from the vulgar world.
translations.idiomatic: The rescript praised the grand instructor's purity, remoteness from ambition, and lifelong integrity.

sentences.zh: 艾服王事，六十餘載，忠肅在公，慮不及私。

translations.literal: For grey-headed decades he served royal affairs; he was loyal and solemn for the public good and gave no thought to private gain.
translations.idiomatic: For more than sixty years he labored for the state with single-minded loyalty.

sentences.zh: 遂應眾舉，曆登三事。

translations.literal: Thus answering the multitude's recommendation he ascended in succession to the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Called upward by consensus, he rose through the three chief posts.

sentences.zh: 仍荷保傅之重，綢繆論道之任，光輔奕世，亮茲天工，迪宣謀猷，弘濟大烈，可謂朝之俊老，眾所具瞻者也。

translations.literal: Still he bore the weight of Tutor and Mentor and the intimate duty of discussing the Way; he brightly aided successive reigns, illumined this heavenly task, opened and spread counsel, and enlarged great merit; he may be called the court's eminent elder whom all behold.
translations.idiomatic: He shouldered tutor duties, shaped policy beside the throne, and guided generations—truly the sage elder the whole court admired.

sentences.zh: 朕昧-{於}-政道，庶事未康，挹仰耆訓，導揚厥蒙，庶賴顯德，緝熙有成。

translations.literal: We are dim in the way of government; myriad affairs are not yet settled; We draw on the teaching of elders and seek to guide Our ignorance; We hope to rely on shining virtue and achieve good order.
translations.idiomatic: We confess dullness in governing; many tasks remain troubled; We lean on venerable counsel to mend Our shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 而公屢以年高疾篤，致仕告退。

translations.literal: Yet the Duke repeatedly, citing advanced age and grave illness, has asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he cites age and illness and begs to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 惟從公志，則朕孰與諮謀？

translations.literal: If We follow the Duke's wish, with whom shall We take counsel?
translations.idiomatic: If We grant his wish, whom shall We consult?

sentences.zh: 譬彼涉川，罔知攸濟。

translations.literal: It is like crossing a river with no knowledge of where to ford.
translations.idiomatic: We would be fording a river with no ford in sight.

sentences.zh: 是用未許，迄-{於}-累載。

translations.literal: Therefore We have not permitted it until many years had passed.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason We denied him year after year.

sentences.zh: 而高讓彌篤，至意難違，覽其盛指，俾朕憮然。

translations.literal: Yet his lofty yielding grows ever more sincere; his utmost intent is hard to refuse; reading his earnest statement fills Us with sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: His modest resolve only deepened; facing his appeal leaves Us torn.

sentences.zh: 夫功成弗有，上德所隆，成人之美，君子與焉。

translations.literal: To achieve merit yet not claim it is what highest virtue exalts; to complete another's excellence is what the gentleman joins in.
translations.idiomatic: Refusing to cling to power crowns supreme virtue; honoring another's wish is the gentleman's way.

sentences.zh: 豈必遂朕憑賴之心，以枉大雅進止之度哉！

translations.literal: How must We satisfy Our reliance on him and wrong the great refinement's measure of advance and withdrawal!
translations.idiomatic: We cannot cling to Our need and violate his noble sense of when to stay or go.

sentences.zh: 今聽其所執，以壽光公就第，位同保傅，在三司之右。

translations.literal: Now We hear what he holds to: let the Duke of Shouguang retire to his mansion with rank equal to Tutor and Mentor, standing to the right of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore let the Duke of Shouguang withdraw home with honors matching the grand tutors and precedence beside the three ministers.

sentences.zh: 公宜頤精養神，保衞太和，以究遐福。

translations.literal: The Duke should nurture essence and spirit, guard supreme harmony, and attain lasting blessing.
translations.idiomatic: May he conserve his strength, preserve inner harmony, and enjoy long felicity.

sentences.zh: 其賜几杖，不朝。

translations.literal: Grant him an armrest and staff and exempt him from court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He receives stool and staff and is freed from court audiences.

sentences.zh: 古之哲王，欽祗國老，憲行乞言，以彌縫其闕。

translations.literal: Ancient wise kings revered state elders, sought words on exemplary conduct, and thereby mended their shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of old honored national elders and solicited advice to repair their rule.

sentences.zh: 若朝有大政，皆就諮之。

translations.literal: Whenever the court has great policies, all shall go to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Major state decisions shall still be brought to him for guidance.

sentences.zh: 又賜安車駟馬，第一區，錢百萬，絹五百匹，床帷簟褥，置舍人六人，官騎二十人，以世子徽爲散騎常侍，使常優遊定省。

translations.literal: Further grant him a comfortable carriage and four horses, one residence, one million cash, five hundred bolts of silk, bed curtains and bamboo mats; assign six household gentlemen and twenty official riders; appoint his heir Hui Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary so that he may often leisurely visit and attend his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He also receives an honorific carriage, a mansion, a million coins, five hundred rolls of silk, bedding, six household attendants, twenty mounted escorts, and his heir Hui is made cavalier attendant-in-ordinary so he may visit his father with ease.

sentences.zh: 祿賜所供，策命儀-{制}-，一如舊典而有加焉。」

translations.literal: Salary and gifts to be supplied, patent and ceremonial regulations—all shall follow the old statutes with additions.
translations.idiomatic: Stipends, patents, and ceremonial detail follow precedent with added largesse.

sentences.zh: 明年薨。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 帝-{於}-朝堂發哀，追贈太傅，賜秘器，朝服，衣一襲，錢三十萬，布百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor expressed mourning in the court hall; posthumously he was advanced to Grand Instructor; he was granted secret burial vessels, a court robe, one suit of clothes, three hundred thousand cash, and one hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign mourned him in the court hall, posthumously restored him as grand instructor, and granted burial gear, court robes, a full suit, three hundred thousand cash, and a hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 諡曰成。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，有司奏，-{沖}-與安平王孚等十二人皆存銘太常，配食-{於}-廟。

translations.literal: Early in Xianning the authorities memorialized that Chong, together with Prince of Anping Sima Fu and eleven others, should all have their names recorded by the Grand Master of Ceremonies and receive sacrifice in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xianning officials asked that Chong and Sima Fu of Anping among twelve men be inscribed at the Ministry of Rites and honored with temple offerings.

sentences.zh: 初，-{沖}-與孫邕、曹羲、荀顗、何晏共集《論語》諸家訓注之善者，記其姓名，因從其義，有不安者輒改易之，名曰《論語集解》。

translations.literal: Initially Chong together with Sun Yong, Cao Xi, Xun Yi, and He Yan jointly assembled the best commentary glosses on the Analects from various scholars, recorded their names, followed their interpretations, and where unsatisfactory promptly revised them; he titled it Collected Explanations of the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Chong joined Sun Yong, Cao Xi, Xun Yi, and He Yan to sift Analects commentaries, credit authors, adopt sound readings, and revise weak points; the work became the Analects Collected Glosses.

sentences.zh: 成，奏之魏朝，-{於}-今傳焉。

translations.literal: When it was completed it was presented to the Wei court and has been transmitted to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Submitted to Wei, it remains standard reading.

sentences.zh: -{沖}-無子，以從子徽爲嗣，位至平原內史。

translations.literal: Chong had no son; he adopted his nephew Hui as heir; Hui rose to Interior Secretary of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, Chong made his nephew Hui heir; Hui reached interior secretary of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 徽卒，子簡嗣。

translations.literal: When Hui died, his son Jian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's son Jian inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 何曾

translations.literal: He Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: Minister He Zeng.

sentences.zh: 何曾，字穎考，陳國陽夏人也。

translations.literal: He Zeng, courtesy Yingkao, was a native of Yangxia in the Chen principality.
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng, styled Yingkao, hailed from Yangxia in Chen.

sentences.zh: 父夔，魏太僕、陽武亭侯。

translations.literal: His father Kui had been Grand Coachman of Wei and Village Marquis of Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kui served Wei as grand coachman with the village marquisate of Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 曾少襲爵，好學博聞，與同郡袁侃齊名。

translations.literal: Zeng in youth inherited the noble rank; he loved learning and was broadly informed; he shared renown in his commandery with Yuan Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Young Zeng inherited the title, pursued wide reading, and matched Yuan Kan in local fame.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝初爲平原侯，曾爲文學。

translations.literal: When Wei Mingdi was first Marquis of Pingyuan, Zeng was his Literary Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: While Mingdi still held the Pingyuan marquisate, Zeng was his literary attendant.

sentences.zh: 及即位，累遷散騎侍郎、汲郡典農中郎將、給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Mingdi ascended the throne, Zeng was repeatedly promoted to Cavalier Gentleman, Diannong Commandant of Ji commandery, and Serving Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Upon Mingdi's accession Zeng rose through cavalry gentleman, agriculture intendant of Ji, and attendant at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「臣聞爲國者以清靜爲基，而百姓以良吏爲本。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial stating that your servant has heard that those who hold the state take quiet simplicity as foundation and that common people take good officials as root.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that rulers rest policy on tranquillity while the people depend on worthy magistrates.

sentences.zh: 今海內虛耗，事役眾多，誠宜恤養黎元，悅以使人。

translations.literal: Now within the Four Seas resources are depleted and corvée duties are many; truly it is fitting to pity and nurture the black-haired multitude and thereby please them when employing them.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm drained and labor endless, he urged pity for the common folk and leadership that wins willing service.

sentences.zh: 郡守之權雖輕，猶專任千里，比之-{於}-古，則列國之君也。

translations.literal: Though the authority of a commandery governor is light, still he holds sole charge of a thousand li; compared with antiquity, he is like the lord of a feudal state.
translations.idiomatic: A prefect wields limited formal power yet governs a vast territory—in ancient terms, the equivalent of a regional ruler.

sentences.zh: 上當奉宣朝恩，以致惠和，下當興利而除其害。

translations.literal: Above he ought to convey and spread court kindness to bring beneficence and harmony; below he ought to promote gain for the people and remove what harms them.
translations.idiomatic: He must voice the court's benevolence so peace spreads below, and actively clear burdens while fostering prosperity.

sentences.zh: 得其人則可安，非其人則爲患。

translations.literal: If the right man is obtained the region can be secure; if not, the wrong man becomes a scourge.
translations.idiomatic: The right appointee brings stability; the wrong one breeds disaster.

sentences.zh: 故漢宣稱曰：「百姓所以安其田里，而無歎息愁恨之心者，政平訟理也。

translations.literal: Therefore Han Xuandi declared: The reason the hundred surnames can rest secure in their fields and lanes without sighing or harboring resentment is that government is even and lawsuits are just.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xuandi once said people live content in their villages when rule is fair and justice is sound.

sentences.zh: 與我共此者，其惟良二千石乎！

translations.literal: Those who share this task with me—are they not the worthy two-thousand-bushel officials!
translations.idiomatic: Only capable governors, he added, share that burden with the throne.

sentences.zh: 」此誠可謂知政之本也。

translations.literal: This may truly be called knowing the root of governance.
translations.idiomatic: That, Zeng concluded, is understanding what truly holds the state together.

sentences.zh: 方今國家大舉，新有發調，軍師遠征，上下劬勞。

translations.literal: Now the state is launching great undertakings; there are new levies and drafts; the army marches far; high and low alike labor exhaustively.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was mobilizing for major campaigns—fresh taxes, long expeditions, and grinding toil at every level.

sentences.zh: 夫百姓可與樂成，難與慮始。

translations.literal: The common people can rejoice with you when success is won but are hard to consult at the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary folk delight in finished projects yet resist every disruptive start.

sentences.zh: 愚惑之人，能厭目前之小勤，而忘爲亂之大禍者，是以郡守益不可不得其人。

translations.literal: Stupid and deluded men may resent slight present exertions and forget the great calamity of rebellion—therefore it is all the more imperative that governors not fail to be the right men.
translations.idiomatic: The foolish resent minor inconvenience and ignore the catastrophe rebellion brings—so choosing prefects matters immensely.

sentences.zh: 才雖難備，猶宜粗有威恩，爲百姓所信憚者。

translations.literal: Though complete talent is hard to gather, still there ought roughly to be both awe and kindness so that the common people trust and fear them.
translations.idiomatic: Perfect officers are rare, yet appointees should command respect and sympathy alike.

sentences.zh: 臣聞諸郡守，有年老或疾病，皆委政丞掾，不恤庶事。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that various governors, being elderly or ill, all delegate administration to assistants and clerks and spare no thought for the myriad tasks of office.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng charged that many aging or sick prefects dumped work on subordinates and ignored public duty.

sentences.zh: 或體性疏怠，不以政理爲意。

translations.literal: Some by disposition are careless and slack and take governing as no concern.
translations.idiomatic: Others were simply lazy and treated administration as optional.

sentences.zh: 在官積年，惠澤不加-{於}-人。

translations.literal: Having remained in office year after year, their kindly moisture does not reach the people.
translations.idiomatic: Years in post brought the populace no tangible benefit.

sentences.zh: 然-{於}-考課之限，罪亦不至詘免。

translations.literal: Yet within the limits of merit review their faults do not reach demotion or dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Annual evaluations still fell short of forcing them out.

sentences.zh: 故得經延歲月，而無斥罷之期。

translations.literal: Therefore they can stretch across months and years with no prospect of removal.
translations.idiomatic: They lingered indefinitely without fear of recall.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以爲可密詔主者，使隱核參訪郡守，其有老病不隱親人物，及宰牧少恩，好修人事，煩撓百姓者，皆可征還，爲更選代。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly thinks a secret edict could order the responsible office secretly to examine governors: those who are old or sick and do not personally oversee human affairs, or who as shepherds show little kindness, favor cultivating personal ties, and harass the common people—all may be summoned back and replaced with newly chosen successors.
translations.idiomatic: He urged confidential audits to recall negligent, cruel, or politically meddling prefects and install better men.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was promoted Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he became cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝將伐遼東，曾上疏魏帝曰：「臣聞先王-{制}-法，必全-{於}-慎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was about to campaign against Liaodong, Zeng submitted a memorial to the Wei emperor stating that your servant has heard former kings, in establishing laws, invariably pursued completeness in caution.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Liaodong expedition Zeng reminded the Wei court that sage kings built institutions on meticulous safeguards.

sentences.zh: 故建官受任，則置副佐；

translations.literal: Therefore when establishing offices and receiving appointees they set deputy assistants;
translations.idiomatic: They paired every chief appointment with a deputy.

sentences.zh: 陳師命將，則立監貳；

translations.literal: When marshaling troops and commissioning generals they established supervisors and seconds;
translations.idiomatic: Field armies received watchdog officers and alternate commanders.

sentences.zh: 宣命遣使，則設介副；

translations.literal: When proclaiming orders and dispatching envoys they set deputies;
translations.idiomatic: Envoys too traveled with ranked backups.

sentences.zh: 臨敵交刃，又參禦右，蓋以盡思謀之功，防安危之變也。

translations.literal: When facing the enemy with blades crossed they also assigned chariot guards on the right—thereby exhausting counsel and planning and guarding against shifts of safety and danger.
translations.idiomatic: Even on the battlefield aides rode beside the commander so counsel flowed and contingencies were covered.

sentences.zh: 是以在險當難，則權足相濟；

translations.literal: Thus when in peril or facing hardship, discretionary authority suffices for mutual rescue;
translations.idiomatic: In crisis such redundancy lets officers rescue one another.

sentences.zh: 隕缺不豫，則才足相代。

translations.literal: When mishap or incapacity strikes, talent suffices to substitute.
translations.idiomatic: If a commander falls, another can step in.

sentences.zh: 其爲國防，至深至遠。

translations.literal: Such arrangements for the state reach profoundly far.
translations.idiomatic: Those layers of redundancy shield the realm at depth.

sentences.zh: 及至漢氏，亦循舊章，韓信伐趙，張耳爲貳；

translations.literal: Down to Han too they followed old regulations: when Han Xin attacked Zhao, Zhang Er served as second;
translations.idiomatic: Han precedents matched: Zhang Er backed Han Xin against Zhao.

sentences.zh: 馬援討越，劉隆副軍。

translations.literal: when Ma Yuan campaigned against the Yue, Liu Long assisted the army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Long supported Ma Yuan's southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 前世之跡，著在篇志。

translations.literal: Traces of earlier ages are set down in documents and records.
translations.idiomatic: History documents each precedent.

sentences.zh: 今太尉奉辭誅罪，精甲銳鋒，歩騎數萬，道路迥阻，且四千里。

translations.literal: Now the Grand Commandant receives the mandate to punish crime; there are elite armor and sharp blades, infantry and cavalry numbering tens of thousands; the route is remote and obstructed—moreover four thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Today's expedition sends crack troops tens of thousands strong over four thousand li of harsh roads.

sentences.zh: 雖假天威，有征無戰，寇或潛遁，消引日月。

translations.literal: Though relying on heavenly majesty there may be expedition without battle, should the foe slip away and hide, days and months may drag on.
translations.idiomatic: Even if intimidation avoids combat, a fleeing enemy could prolong the march indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 命無常期，人非金石，遠慮詳備，誠宜有副。

translations.literal: Fate has no fixed term; men are not metal or stone; far-sighted thorough preparation truly calls for a deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Mortality is uncertain; prudent planning demands a second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 今北軍諸將及太尉所督，皆爲僚屬，名位不殊，素無定分統御之尊，卒有變急，不相鎮攝。

translations.literal: Now the northern army's commanders and those under the Grand Commandant's direction are all staff colleagues; names and ranks are not distinguished; ordinarily there is no fixed hierarchy of command; should sudden crisis arise, they will not restrain one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yet every colonel now shares equal standing under the grand commandant, so sudden emergencies would lack a clear chain of control.

sentences.zh: 存不忘亡，聖達所裁。

translations.literal: While surviving, not forgetting perishing—this the enlightened sage regulates.
translations.idiomatic: The wise plan for disaster even in safety.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以爲宜選大臣名將威重宿著者，成其禮秩，遣詣北軍，進同謀略，退爲副佐。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly thinks it fitting to select a great minister or famed general of proven awe and long-standing reputation, complete his ceremonial rank, and dispatch him to the northern army: advancing, join in planning; retreating, serve as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng proposed attaching a senior minister-general to coordinate strategy and serve as understudy.

sentences.zh: 雖有萬一不虞之變，軍主有儲，則無患矣。

translations.literal: Though there be the slightest chance of unexpected change, if the army chief has reserve, there will be no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Even rare contingencies would find the column prepared.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rejected the advice.

sentences.zh: 出補河內太守，在任有威嚴之稱。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Henei and in office gained a reputation for awe and severity.
translations.idiomatic: As Henei prefect he earned a name for stern authority.

sentences.zh: 徵拜侍中，母憂去官。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Palace Attendant; mourning for his mother removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant followed, then maternal mourning forced resignation.

sentences.zh: 嘉平中，爲司隸校尉。

translations.literal: In the Jiaping era he was Metropolitan Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiaping he became metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 撫軍校事尹模憑寵作威，奸利盈積，朝野畏憚，莫敢言者。

translations.literal: Army Inspector Yin Mo relied on imperial favor to throw his weight around; illicit profits piled up; court and countryside feared him and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Yin Mo abused favor to enrich himself and silence critics.

sentences.zh: 曾奏劾之，朝廷稱焉。

translations.literal: Zeng memorialized to impeach him; the court praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng impeached him and won court applause.

sentences.zh: 時曹爽專權，宣帝稱疾，曾亦謝病。

translations.literal: At the time Cao Shuang monopolized power; Emperor Xuan feigned illness; Zeng also pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Shuang dominated, Sima Yi played sick—and so did Zeng.

sentences.zh: 爽誅，乃起視事，魏帝之廢也，曾預其謀焉。

translations.literal: When Shuang was executed he then resumed duties; at the Wei emperor's deposition Zeng took part in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuang fell Zeng returned to duty and helped depose Cao Fang.

sentences.zh: 時歩兵校尉阮籍負才放誕，居喪無禮。

translations.literal: At the time Infantry Commandant Ruan Ji, trusting his talent, behaved recklessly and observed mourning without ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Infantry commandant Ruan Ji flaunted genius and scandalized mourners.

sentences.zh: 曾面質籍-{於}-文帝座曰：「卿縱情背禮，敗俗之人，今忠賢執政，綜核名實，若卿之曹，不可長也。

translations.literal: Zeng confronted Ji before Emperor Wen's seat, saying: You indulge emotion and betray ritual; you are one who ruins custom. Now loyal worthies hold power and examine names against reality; men of your sort cannot long endure.
translations.idiomatic: Before Sima Zhao he accused Ruan Ji of flouting mourning rites and corrupting morals.

sentences.zh: 」因言-{於}-帝曰：「公方以孝治天下，而聽阮籍以重哀飲酒食肉-{於}-公座。

translations.literal: He therefore spoke to the emperor: You propose to rule the realm by filial piety, yet you permit Ruan Ji amid deep mourning to drink wine and eat meat in your presence.
translations.idiomatic: He protested that allowing banqueting during deep mourning mocked the claim to rule by filial piety.

sentences.zh: 宜擯四裔，無令污染華夏。

translations.literal: He ought to be banished to the four peripheries and not be allowed to defile the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng demanded banishment lest Ji stain the heartland.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此子羸病若此，君不能爲吾忍邪！

translations.literal: The emperor said: This fellow is so wasted by illness—can you not bear with him for my sake!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao replied that Ji was too frail to punish harshly.

sentences.zh: 」曾重引據，辭理甚切。

translations.literal: Zeng cited precedent again; his argument was very pointed.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng pressed legal precedent with biting logic.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不從，時人敬憚之。

translations.literal: Though the emperor did not comply, people of the time respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince refused, yet contemporaries stood in awe of Zeng.

sentences.zh: 毌丘儉誅，子甸、妻荀應坐死。

translations.literal: When Guanqiu Jian was executed, his son Dian and wife Lady Xun were liable to collective death sentences.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian's fall condemned his son Dian and Lady Xun to kin punishment.

sentences.zh: 其族兄顗、族父虞並景帝姻通，共表魏帝以丐其命。

translations.literal: His clan elder brother Yi and clan uncle Yu were both related by marriage to Emperor Jing; jointly they petitioned the Wei emperor to spare their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen tied to Sima Shi begged clemency.

sentences.zh: 詔聽離婚，荀所生女芝爲潁川太守劉子元妻，亦坐死，以懷妊繫獄。

translations.literal: An edict permitted divorce; a daughter born to Lady Xun, Zhi, was wife of Yingchuan Administrator Liu Ziyuan and also faced death; being pregnant she was held in prison.
translations.idiomatic: A decree allowed divorce to spare some kin, yet pregnant daughter Zhi—wife of Liu Ziyuan—remained jailed for execution.

sentences.zh: 荀辭詣曾乞恩曰：「芝系在廷尉，顧影知命，計日備法。

translations.literal: Lady Xun went to Zeng begging grace, saying: Zhi is bound at the commandant of justice; watching her shadow she knows her fate; she counts the days until the law takes her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xun appealed to Zeng, describing her daughter counting down to execution.

sentences.zh: 乞沒爲官婢，以贖芝命。

translations.literal: I beg to be confiscated as a government slave to ransom Zhi's life.
translations.idiomatic: She offered herself as a state slave to redeem Zhi.

sentences.zh: 」曾哀之，騰辭上議。

translations.literal: Zeng pitied her and forwarded the plea with his recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Zeng forwarded a compassionate memorial.

sentences.zh: 朝廷僉以爲當，遂改法。

translations.literal: The court unanimously deemed it right and therefore revised the law.
translations.idiomatic: Officials agreed and amended the statute.

sentences.zh: 語在《刑法志》。

translations.literal: The matter is recorded in the Treatise on Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Details appear in the Jin Treatise on Law.

sentences.zh: 曾在司隸積年，遷尚書，正元年中爲鎮北將軍、都督河北諸軍事、假節。

translations.literal: Zeng having been Metropolitan Commandant for years was promoted Master of Writing; in the Zhengyuan era he was General Who Conquers the North, Area Commander-in-Chief of Hebei military affairs, with credential.
translations.idiomatic: After long service as metropolitan commandant he rose to minister of writing, then northern commander over Hebei with imperial credentials.

sentences.zh: 將之鎮，文帝使武帝、齊王攸辭送數十里。

translations.literal: When about to depart to his command, Emperor Wen sent Emperor Wu and Prince of Qi Sima You to take leave and escort him for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao sent his sons Sima Yan and Sima You to escort him dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 曾盛爲賓主，備太牢之饌。

translations.literal: Zeng lavishly acted as host and guest and prepared a feast of the full ox sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng staged an elaborate banquet with a grand sacrifice spread.

sentences.zh: 侍從吏騶，莫不醉飽。

translations.literal: Attending clerks and outriders—none failed to get drunk and full.
translations.idiomatic: Every attendant rode away stuffed and drunk.

sentences.zh: 帝既出，又過其子劭。

translations.literal: After the emperor had departed, he also visited his son Shao.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial party then stopped at Zeng's son Shao.

sentences.zh: 曾先敕劭曰：「客必過汝，汝當豫嚴。

translations.literal: Zeng had earlier instructed Shao: Guests are sure to pass by you; you must prepare strictly beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng had warned Shao to ready himself because guests would call.

sentences.zh: 」劭不冠帶，停帝良久，曾深以譴劭。

translations.literal: Shao did not don cap and belt; he detained the emperor a long time; Zeng sternly rebuked Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Shao received them without full dress and prolonged the visit; Zeng scolded him harshly.

sentences.zh: 曾見崇重如此。

translations.literal: Thus Zeng was honored and esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor Zeng commanded.

sentences.zh: 遷征北將軍，進封潁昌鄕侯。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Campaigns the North and advanced to Village Marquis of Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: He moved up to general who campaigns the north and village marquis of Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 咸熙初，拜司徒，改封郎陵侯。

translations.literal: Early in the Xianxi era he was appointed Minister of Education and his fief changed to Marquis of Langling.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xianxi he became minister of education with the Langling marquisate.

sentences.zh: 文帝爲晉王，曾與高柔、鄭-{沖}-俱爲三公，將入見，曾獨致拜盡敬，二人猶揖而已。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was Prince of Jin, Zeng together with Gao Rou and Zheng Chong were all Three Dukes; about to enter audience, Zeng alone performed full obeisance with utmost respect; the two others merely bowed.
translations.idiomatic: As Jin prince, Sima Zhao stood with three dukes: only Zeng dropped to full prostration while Gao Rou and Zheng Chong bowed.

sentences.zh: 武帝襲王位，以曾爲晉丞相，加侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu inherited the princedom he made Zeng chancellor of Jin and added Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan made him Jin chancellor with palace attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 與裴秀、王沈等勸進。

translations.literal: Together with Pei Xiu and Wang Shen he urged the advance to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: With Pei Xiu and Wang Shen he pressed the succession.

sentences.zh: 踐阼，拜太尉，進爵爲公，食邑千八百戸。

translations.literal: When Wu ascended the throne he was appointed Grand Commandant, advanced to duke, fief of one thousand eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At Jin accession he became grand commandant and duke over eighteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，詔曰：「蓋謨明弼諧，王躬是保，所以宣崇大訓，克咸四海也。

translations.literal: Early in Taishi an edict stated: Planning clarity and assistant harmony preserve the king's person—thereby propagating great instruction and bringing the Four Seas to completion.
translations.idiomatic: A Taishi edict praised ministers who harmonize policy and shelter the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 侍中、太尉何曾，立德高峻，執心忠亮，博物洽聞，明識弘達，翼佐先皇，勳庸顯著。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant He Zeng established virtue lofty and steep; his heart is loyal and bright; broad learning and comprehensive hearing; perspicacious knowledge vast attainment; he aided the former emperor and his merit was manifest.
translations.idiomatic: It hailed Zeng as upright, learned, and foundational to the prior reign.

sentences.zh: 朕纂洪業，首相王室。

translations.literal: We have inherited the great enterprise and head the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor claimed the mandate and led the house of Jin.

sentences.zh: 迪惟前人，施-{於}-朕躬。

translations.literal: He opens the way for former men and applies it to Our person.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng extended those models to the new sovereign.

sentences.zh: 實佐命興化，光贊政道。

translations.literal: Truly he aided the Mandate and raised transformation; he brightly assists the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: He had stabilized the succession and enlightened governance.

sentences.zh: 夫三司之任，雖左右王事，若乃予違汝弼，匡獎不逮，則存平保傅。

translations.literal: Though the Three Offices' charge assists the king's affairs left and right, as for correcting Our faults and supplying Our lacks, that rests with Tutor and Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: High ministers aid daily rule, yet correcting the throne belongs to tutors.

sentences.zh: 故將明袞職，未如用乂厥-{辟}-之重。

translations.literal: Therefore when clarifying robe-and-cap duties, nothing matches the weight of supporting the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: No dignity outweighs guiding the ruler himself.

sentences.zh: 其以曾爲太保，侍中如故。

translations.literal: Let Zeng be Grand Tutor; Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng was named grand tutor while keeping palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 」久之，以本官領司徒。

translations.literal: After a long while, in his original office he concurrently headed the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Later he added concurrent stewardship of the ministry of education.

sentences.zh: 曾固讓，不許。

translations.literal: Zeng firmly declined; not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He resisted; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 遣散騎常侍諭旨，乃視事。

translations.literal: A Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary was sent to convey the intent; then he attended to duties.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy explained the command until he accepted the posts.

sentences.zh: 進位太傅。

translations.literal: He advanced to Grand Instructor.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion followed to grand instructor.

sentences.zh: 曾以老年，屢乞遜位。

translations.literal: Zeng, on account of old age, repeatedly begged to yield position.
translations.idiomatic: Age drove repeated resignation bids.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「太傅明朗高亮，執心弘毅，可謂舊德老成，國之宗臣者也。

translations.literal: The edict stated: The Grand Instructor is bright, perspicuous, lofty, and shining; his heart is great and resolute; he may be called an old virtue mature—the state's pillar minister.
translations.idiomatic: A rescript called him the dynasty's senior pillar.

sentences.zh: 而高尚其事，屢辭祿位。

translations.literal: Yet he esteems withdrawal and repeatedly declines salary and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he kept seeking retirement.

sentences.zh: 朕以寡德，憑賴保佑，省覽章表，實用憮然。

translations.literal: We, of scant virtue, rely on his protection; reading his petitions truly fills Us with sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor confessed reliance and sorrow at each refusal.

sentences.zh: 雖欲成人之美，豈得遂其雅志，而忘翼佐之益哉！

translations.literal: Though We wish to complete another's excellence, how can We satisfy his refined intent and forget the benefit of his assistance!
translations.idiomatic: Honoring his wish could not outweigh losing his counsel.

sentences.zh: 又司徒所掌務煩，不可久勞耆艾。

translations.literal: Moreover the Minister of Education's charge is vexatiously busy; he cannot long weary an elder.
translations.idiomatic: Education portfolios exhaust men too old for such labor.

sentences.zh: 其進太宰，侍中如故。

translations.literal: Advance him to Grand Duke; Palace Attendant as before.
