translations.idiomatic: Zeng became grand duke while retaining palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 朝會劍履乘輿上殿，如漢相國蕭何、田千秋、魏太傅鍾繇故事。

translations.literal: At court meetings sword and shoes, riding the carriage and ascending the hall—according to the precedents of Han Chancellor Xiao He, Tian Qianqiu, and Wei Grand Instructor Zhong Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Court privileges matched Xiao He, Tian Qianqiu, and Zhong Yao—sword in hall and carriage to the steps.

sentences.zh: 賜錢百萬，絹五百匹及八尺床帳簟褥自副。

translations.literal: Granted one million cash, five hundred bolts of silk, and eight-foot bed curtains, bamboo mats, and bedding in duplicate.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts included a million coins, five hundred bolts of silk, and paired bedding sets.

sentences.zh: 置長史掾屬祭酒及員吏，一依舊-{制}-。

translations.literal: Establish chief clerk, staff, libationer, and clerks according to old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Staffing followed ancient tables for clerks and libationers.

sentences.zh: 所給親兵官騎如前。

translations.literal: Personal guards and official riders supplied as before.
translations.idiomatic: Bodyguard complements stayed unchanged.

sentences.zh: 主者依次按禮典，務使優備。

translations.literal: Let those in charge follow ritual canons in order and strive to make provision generous and complete.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaus were told to supply him lavishly per statute.

sentences.zh: 」-{後}-每召見，敕以常所飲食服物自隨，令二子侍從。

translations.literal: Afterward at each summons he was instructed to bring his usual food, drink, and clothing; he was ordered to have two sons attend.
translations.idiomatic: Later audiences let him bring familiar fare and clothing with two sons in attendance.

sentences.zh: 薨，時年八十。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty.

sentences.zh: 帝-{於}-朝堂素服舉哀，賜東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，錢三十萬，布百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor in the court hall wore unlined mourning and expressed mourning; granted eastern park secret vessels, one set court robe, one suit of clothes, three hundred thousand cash, one hundred bolts cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign mourned in white at court, gifting burial gear, court dress, cash, and cloth.

sentences.zh: 將葬，下禮官議諡。

translations.literal: When about to bury, the throne ordered ritual officials to deliberate posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Burial preparations opened debate on his posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 博士秦秀諡爲「繆醜」，帝不從，策諡曰孝。

translations.literal: Erudite Qin Xiu proposed the posthumous appellation Warped and Ugly; the emperor did not follow this and by patent gave the posthumous title Filial.
translations.idiomatic: Doctor Qin Xiu urged the harsh epithet Warped and Vile; the throne overruled him and canonized Zeng as Filial.

sentences.zh: 太康末，子劭自表改諡爲元。

translations.literal: Late in the Taikang era son Shao personally petitioned to change the posthumous title to Primogen.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Taikang his son Shao won approval to restyle him as Primogen.

sentences.zh: 曾性至孝，閨門整肅，自少及長，無聲樂嬖幸之好。

translations.literal: By nature Zeng was utmost filial; within his inner quarters discipline was strict; from youth to age he had no fondness for music or favored intimates.
translations.idiomatic: He was famously dutiful toward kin and kept an orderly household, eschewing musicians and concubinal distraction.

sentences.zh: 年老之-{後}-，與妻相見，皆正衣冠，相待如賓。

translations.literal: After growing old, whenever he met his wife they always straightened cap and robes and treated each other like guests.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he and his wife greeted each other fully dressed, with grave courtesy.

sentences.zh: 己南向，妻北面，再拜上酒，酬酢既畢便出。

translations.literal: He faced south, his wife faced north; they twice bowed and offered wine; when the toast ritual finished they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed in opposing directions, exchanged ritual cups, then parted.

sentences.zh: 一歲如此者不過再三焉。

translations.literal: In a year such occasions occurred no more than two or three times.
translations.idiomatic: They repeated this formal audience only a handful of times yearly.

sentences.zh: 初，司隸校尉傅玄著論稱曾及荀顗曰：「以文王之道事其親者，其潁昌何侯乎，其荀侯乎！

translations.literal: Initially Metropolitan Commandant Fu Xuan wrote a discourse praising Zeng and Xun Yi, saying: Those who serve their kin by King Wen's Way—are they not Marquis He of Yingchang and Marquis Xun!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan once ranked Zeng alongside Xun Yi as paragons of filial devotion patterned on King Wen.

sentences.zh: 古稱曾、閔，今日荀、何。

translations.literal: The ancients praised Zeng and Min; today we have Xun and He.
translations.idiomatic: Classical ages hailed Zeng Shen and Min Sun; Fu paired them with Xun and He.

sentences.zh: 內盡其心以事其親，外崇禮讓以接天下。

translations.literal: Within they exhaust their hearts to serve their kin; without they elevate ritual deference in dealing with all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: They cherished parents inwardly while outwardly modeling humility toward the world.

sentences.zh: 孝子，百世之宗；

translations.literal: Filial sons are the lineage anchors for a hundred generations;
translations.idiomatic: True sons anchor a clan across centuries.

sentences.zh: 仁人，天下之命。

translations.literal: Humane men are the mandate of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Humane ministers sustain the realm.

sentences.zh: 有能行孝之道，君子之儀錶也。

translations.literal: Those able to practice the Way of filial piety are the models for gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone mastering filial duty becomes a moral exemplar.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「高山仰止，景行行止。

translations.literal: The Odes say: High mountains are looked up to; great roads are walked upon.
translations.idiomatic: As the Odes sing, great peaks invite reverence and broad paths invite emulation.

sentences.zh: 」令德不遵二夫子之景行者，非樂中正之道也。

translations.literal: Those who do not follow the exemplary conduct of these two masters do not delight in the Way of centrality and correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever spurns such exemplars turns from the balanced path.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「荀、何，君子之宗也。

translations.literal: He further said: Xun and He are the lineage anchors for gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Fu added that Xun and He stood as moral pillars.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「潁昌侯之事親，其盡孝子之道乎！

translations.literal: He further said: In serving kin Marquis Yingchang exhausts the Way of the filial son!
translations.idiomatic: He insisted Zeng embodied complete filial practice.

sentences.zh: 存盡其和，事盡其敬，亡盡其哀，予-{於}-潁昌侯見之矣。

translations.literal: While alive he achieves utmost harmony; in service utmost reverence; in mourning utmost grief—I have seen this in Marquis Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu saw perfect harmony in life, reverence in duty, and grief in mourning.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「見其親之黨，如見其親，六十而孺慕，予-{於}-潁昌侯見之矣。

translations.literal: He further said: Seeing his kin's kin is like seeing his kin; at sixty still cherishing childlike longing—I have seen this in Marquis Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Even toward collateral kin Zeng showed parental tenderness well past sixty.

sentences.zh: 」然性奢豪，務在華侈。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was extravagant and proud and pursued splendor and luxury.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zeng loved ostentation.

sentences.zh: 帷帳車服，窮極綺麗，廚膳滋味，過-{於}-王者。

translations.literal: Curtains, carriages, and attire were extravagantly ornate; kitchen fare surpassed even kings.
translations.idiomatic: His hangings, coaches, and cuisine outdid royal standards.

sentences.zh: 每燕見，不食太官所設，帝輒命取其食。

translations.literal: Whenever granted informal audience he did not eat what the Royal Kitchen provided; the emperor always ordered his own food brought.
translations.idiomatic: At informal palace meals he refused imperial kitchens and ate only dishes fetched from his mansion.

sentences.zh: 蒸餅上不坼作十字不食。

translations.literal: Steamed cakes whose tops were not split in a cross he would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: He rejected buns unless their crust bore the ritual cross split.

sentences.zh: 食日萬錢，猶曰無下箸處。

translations.literal: Though daily meals cost ten thousand cash he still said there was nowhere worthy to place chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: He spent fortunes on dinner yet complained nothing suited his chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 人以小紙爲書者，敕記室勿報。

translations.literal: If people wrote letters on small scraps he instructed his secretary office not to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Notes on stingy scraps went unanswered by order.

sentences.zh: 劉毅等數劾奏曾侈忲無度，帝以其重臣，一無所問。

translations.literal: Liu Yi and others repeatedly impeached Zeng for unrestrained extravagance; because he was a senior minister the emperor questioned nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated memorials from Liu Yi about Zeng's excess drew no sanction.

sentences.zh: 都官從事劉享嘗奏曾華侈，以銅鉤𦓗紖車，瑩牛蹄角。

translations.literal: Capital Affairs Investigator Liu Xiang once memorialized that Zeng's splendor included bronze harness hooks and straps on his carriage and polished ox hooves and horns.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang cited bronze carriage fittings and lacquered ox hooves as proof of Zeng's waste.

sentences.zh: -{後}-曾-{辟}-享爲掾，或勸勿應，享謂至公之體，不以私憾，遂應-{辟}-。

translations.literal: Later when Zeng summoned Xiang as clerk, some urged him not to accept; Xiang held that the substance of utmost impartiality does not heed private spite, and therefore answered the summons.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng later hired him, Xiang accepted despite warnings, citing public duty over grudges.

sentences.zh: 曾常因小事加享杖罰。

translations.literal: Zeng often over petty matters increased Xiang's punishment with the rod.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng then caned him repeatedly for trifles.

sentences.zh: 其外寬內忌，亦此類也。

translations.literal: Outwardly broad yet inwardly resentful—this too was of that sort.
translations.idiomatic: Outward leniency masked vindictiveness.

sentences.zh: 時司空賈充權擬人主，曾卑充而附之。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of Works Jia Chong wielded power rivaling the ruler; Zeng humbled himself before Chong and attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng courted all-powerful Jia Chong.

sentences.zh: 及充與庾純因酒相競，曾議黨充而抑純，以此爲正直所非。

translations.literal: When Chong and Yu Chun quarreled over wine, Zeng sided with Chong and suppressed Chun—thereby inviting censure from men of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He backed Chong against Yu Chun and lost moral standing.

sentences.zh: 二子：遵、劭。

translations.literal: Two sons: Zun and Shao.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zun and Shao.

sentences.zh: 劭嗣。

translations.literal: Shao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was Shao.

translations.literal: The line consists of a single equals sign.
translations.idiomatic: A lone equals mark stands in the received text.

sentences.zh: 曾子 劭

translations.literal: He Zeng's son Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, son of He Zeng.

translations.literal: The line consists of a single equals sign.
translations.idiomatic: A lone equals mark stands in the received text.

sentences.zh: 劭字敬祖，少與武帝同年，有總角之好。

translations.literal: Shao, courtesy Jingzu, in youth was the same age as Emperor Wu and they had childhood friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He Shao, styled Jingzu, grew up as Sima Yan's age-mate and boyhood friend.

sentences.zh: 帝爲王太子，以劭爲中庶子。

translations.literal: When the emperor was heir apparent he appointed Shao Household Mentor of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: As crown prince Sima Yan named him junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 及即位，轉散騎常侍，甚見親待。

translations.literal: When Wu ascended the throne Shao was transferred Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: At accession Shao became cavalier attendant-in-ordinary with intimate trust.

sentences.zh: 劭雅有姿望，遠客朝見，必以劭侍直。

translations.literal: Shao carried distinguished bearing; whenever distant guests came to court audience the emperor always ordered Shao on duty.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign envoys always met Shao standing attendance.

sentences.zh: 每諸方貢獻，帝輒賜之，而觀其占謝焉。

translations.literal: Whenever various regions offered tribute the emperor habitually gifted Shao and watched them compose thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Regional gifts were rerouted to Shao while the throne watched his courteous replies.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，有司奏劭及兄遵等受故鬲令袁毅貨，雖經赦宥，宜皆禁止。

translations.literal: Early in Xianning authorities memorialized that Shao and elder brother Zun had accepted goods from former Magistrate of Ge Yuan Yi; though amnesty had covered them all alike should be barred from office.
translations.idiomatic: A bribery scandal tied Shao and Zun to Yuan Yi despite prior amnesty.

sentences.zh: 事下廷尉。

translations.literal: The matter went down to the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: The case landed at the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「太保與毅有累世之交，遵等所取差薄，一皆置之。

translations.literal: An edict stated: The Grand Tutor had generations-old ties with Yuan Yi; what Zun and others took was comparatively slight—let all be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor waived penalties citing old friendship and modest bribes.

sentences.zh: 」遷侍中尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted Palace Attendant and Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to palace attendant atop the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，初建東宮，太子年幼，欲令親萬-{機}-，故盛選六傅，以劭爲太子太師，通省尚書事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui ascended, as the Eastern Palace was first established the heir was young and they wished him to grasp myriad affairs; therefore they lavishly chose six tutors and appointed Shao Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent with concurrent oversight of Masters of Writing business.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's reign opened with a packed tutor college for the young crown prince; Shao directed him as grand tutor while coordinating ministry workflow.

sentences.zh: -{後}-轉特進，累遷尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted Esteemed Emeritus and repeatedly rose to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to eminent senior status and left vice presidency of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 劭博學，善屬文，陳説近代事，若指諸掌。

translations.literal: Shao was broadly learned and skilled at composing texts; narrating recent affairs he was as clear as pointing at his palm.
translations.idiomatic: His essays and command of recent history were famously lucid.

sentences.zh: 永康初，遷司徒。

translations.literal: Early in the Yongkang era he was promoted Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Yongkang brought appointment as minister of education.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫篡位，以劭爲太宰。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao of Zhao usurped the throne he appointed Shao Grand Duke.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Lun named him grand duke during the coup.

sentences.zh: 及三王交爭，劭以軒冕而遊其間，無怨之者。

translations.literal: When the three princes contended Shao moved among them in full regalia yet none bore him malice.
translations.idiomatic: Amid civil war he glided between factions unharmed.

sentences.zh: 而驕奢簡貴，亦有父風。

translations.literal: Yet arrogant, luxurious, aloof, and proud—he too had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: He shared his father's haughty extravagance.

sentences.zh: 衣裘服玩，新故巨積。

translations.literal: Furs, robes, and curios—new and old—piled mountain-high.
translations.idiomatic: Wardrobes overflowed with luxuries.

sentences.zh: 食必盡四方珍異，一日之供以錢二萬爲限。

translations.literal: Meals had to exhaust rare delicacies from the four directions; a single day's provision was capped at twenty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Daily banquets budgeted twenty thousand coins for exotic ingredients.

sentences.zh: 時論以爲太官禦膳，無以加之。

translations.literal: Opinion at the time held that even the royal kitchen could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Gossip said palace chefs could not compete.

sentences.zh: 然優遊自足，不貪權勢。

translations.literal: Yet he lounged content and did not covet power.
translations.idiomatic: Still he avoided political ambition.

sentences.zh: 嘗語鄕人王詮曰：「僕雖名位過幸，少無可書之事，惟與夏侯長容諫授博士，可傳史冊耳。

translations.literal: He once told fellow townsman Wang Quan: Though my fame and rank exceed what I deserve, in youth I had nothing worth recording save remonstrating with Xiahou Zhangrong against appointing him erudite—that alone might enter the histories.
translations.idiomatic: He told Wang Quan his sole worthy deed was blocking Xiahou Zhan's doctorate appointment.

sentences.zh: 」所撰《荀粲》、《王弼傳》及諸奏議文章並行-{於}-世。

translations.literal: His compositions—the biographies of Xun Can and Wang Bi plus memorials and essays—circulated together in the age.
translations.idiomatic: His Xun Can and Wang Bi biographies and state papers stayed in circulation.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司徒，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously honored Minister of Education; posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died canonized Kang with posthumous ministry honors.

sentences.zh: 子岐嗣。

translations.literal: Son Qi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His heir was Qi.

sentences.zh: 劭初亡，袁粲吊岐，岐辭以疾。

translations.literal: When Shao first died Yuan Can condoled Qi; Qi declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can visited mourning Qi who pleaded sickness.

sentences.zh: 粲獨哭而出曰：「今年決下婢子品。

translations.literal: Can alone wept leaving and said: This year they will surely downgrade the servant-girl grade.
translations.idiomatic: Can predicted inspectors would humble Qi's clan rating.

sentences.zh: 」王詮謂之曰：「知死吊死，何必見生！

translations.literal: Wang Quan told him: Mourning the dead need not require seeing the living!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quan said condolence did not require an audience.

sentences.zh: 岐前多罪，爾時不下，何公新亡，便下岐品。

translations.literal: Qi earlier had many faults; then they did not lower him; now that Lord He has newly died they immediately downgrade Qi's grade.
translations.idiomatic: He noted hypocrisy: Qi escaped demotion until Zeng's death triggered punishment.

sentences.zh: 人謂中正畏強易弱。

translations.literal: People said the regional investigator feared the mighty and bullied the weak.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers accused favoritism toward the powerful.

sentences.zh: 」粲乃止。

translations.literal: Can then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Can fell silent.

translations.literal: The line consists of a single equals sign.
translations.idiomatic: A lone equals mark stands in the received text.

sentences.zh: 劭庶兄 遵

translations.literal: Shao's elder half-brother Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Zun, elder half-brother of Shao on the distaff side.

translations.literal: The line consists of a single equals sign.
translations.idiomatic: A lone equals mark stands in the received text.

sentences.zh: 遵字思祖，劭庶兄也。

translations.literal: Zun, courtesy Sizu, was Shao's elder half-brother.
translations.idiomatic: He Zun, styled Sizu, was Shao's senior half-brother.

sentences.zh: 少有幹能。

translations.literal: In youth he had administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: He showed early bureaucratic talent.

sentences.zh: 起家散騎黃門郎、散騎常侍、侍中，累轉大鴻臚。

translations.literal: He rose from office Gentleman of the Yellow Gates for Cavalier Attendants, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Palace Attendant, and was repeatedly transferred to Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: His career ran through yellow-gate posts to grand herald.

sentences.zh: 性亦奢忲，役使禦府工匠作禁物，又鬻行器，爲司隸劉毅所奏，免官。

translations.literal: His nature was likewise extravagant and proud; he employed imperial workshop craftsmen to make forbidden objects and also sold traveling gear; Metropolitan Commandant Liu Yi memorialized him and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He forced palace artisans to craft illicit luxuries and peddled travel gear until Liu Yi impeached him out of office.

sentences.zh: 太康初，起爲魏郡太守，遷太僕卿，又免官，卒-{於}-家，四子，嵩、綏、-{機}-、羨。

translations.literal: Early in Taikang he was reappointed Administrator of Wei commandery, promoted Grand Coachman, again dismissed, and died at home; four sons: Song, Sui, Ji, Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang restored him to Wei prefect and grand coachman until another dismissal; he died at home leaving four sons.

translations.literal: The line consists of two equals signs in succession.
translations.idiomatic: A double equals mark stands in the received text.

sentences.zh: 遵子 嵩

translations.literal: Zun's son Song.
translations.idiomatic: Song, son of Zun.

sentences.zh: 嵩字泰基，寬弘愛士，博觀墳籍，尤善《史》、《漢》。

translations.literal: Song, courtesy Taiji, was broad-minded and cherished scholars; he widely perused tombs and archives and especially excelled at the Records and Han histories.
translations.idiomatic: He Song loved books and mastered the Shiji and Hanshu.

sentences.zh: 少曆清官，領著作郎。

translations.literal: In youth he successively held pure offices and headed editorial secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed through clean posts to supervising editor.

sentences.zh: 遵子 綏

translations.literal: Zun's son Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Sui, son of Zun.

sentences.zh: 綏字伯蔚，位至侍中尚書。

translations.literal: Sui, courtesy Boyu, rose to Palace Attendant and Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He Sui reached palace attendant and minister of writing.

sentences.zh: 自以繼世名貴，奢侈過度，性既輕物，翰劄簡傲。

translations.literal: Trusting inherited noble fame he exceeded all bounds in luxury; his nature belittled others and his letters were curt and arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Noble birth bred extravagance, contempt, and supercilious correspondence.

sentences.zh: 城陽王尼見綏書疏，謂人曰：「伯蔚居亂而矜豪乃爾，豈其免乎！

translations.literal: Prince of Chengyang Wang Ni, seeing Sui's notes, told others: Boyu living in chaos yet flaunts pride thus—how can he escape harm!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ni warned that swagger amid turmoil courted disaster.

sentences.zh: 」劉輿、潘滔譖之-{於}-東海王越，越遂誅綏。

translations.literal: Liu Yu and Pan Tao slandered him to Prince of Donghai Sima Yue; Yue then executed Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu and Pan Tao poisoned Sima Yue against him and secured his execution.

sentences.zh: 初，曾侍武帝宴，退而告遵等曰：「國家應天受禪，創業垂統。

translations.literal: Initially when Zeng attended Emperor Wu's banquet he withdrew and told Zun and others: The state received the Mandate from Heaven and founded an enterprise to hand down.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Zeng told sons the dynasty had won heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 吾每宴見，未嘗聞經國遠圖，惟説平生常事，非貽厥孫謀之兆也。

translations.literal: Each banquet audience I never hear far-reaching plans for ordering the realm—only chat about ordinary life; this is no omen of leaving counsel for grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet palace feasts discussed trivia, not statecraft—a bad sign for heirs.

sentences.zh: 及身而已，-{後}-嗣其殆乎！

translations.literal: It ends with our generation—will later heirs not be imperiled!
translations.idiomatic: He feared the line would end with their generation.

sentences.zh: 此子孫之憂也。

translations.literal: This is worry for sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: He foresaw peril for descendants.

sentences.zh: 汝等猶可獲沒。

translations.literal: Yet you may still die a natural death.
translations.idiomatic: Sons might at least die peacefully.

sentences.zh: 」指諸孫曰：「此等必遇亂亡也。

translations.literal: Pointing at grandsons he said: These will surely meet turmoil and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: He predicted chaos for the grandchildren.

sentences.zh: 」及綏死，嵩哭之曰；

translations.literal: When Sui died Song wept for him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At Sui's death Song sobbed:

sentences.zh: 「我祖其大聖乎！」

translations.literal: My grandfather was surely a great sage!
translations.idiomatic: Our grandfather must have been clairvoyant!

sentences.zh: 遵子 -{機}-

translations.literal: Zun's son Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, son of Zun.

sentences.zh: -{機}-爲鄒平令。

translations.literal: Ji served as magistrate of Zouping.
translations.idiomatic: He Ji governed Zouping county.

sentences.zh: 性亦矜傲，責鄕里謝鯤等拜。

translations.literal: His nature was likewise arrogant; he demanded village worthies such as Xie Kun bow to him.
translations.idiomatic: He forced locals like Xie Kun into obeisance.

sentences.zh: 或戒之曰：「禮敬年爵，以德爲主。

translations.literal: Someone admonished him: Ritual respect for age and rank rests on virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said deference should follow virtue, not coercion.

sentences.zh: 令鯤拜勢，懼傷風俗。

translations.literal: Making Kun bow to power harms custom.
translations.idiomatic: Coercing Kun wounded public morals.

sentences.zh: 」-{機}-不以爲慚。

translations.literal: Ji felt no shame.
translations.idiomatic: Ji remained unrepentant.

sentences.zh: 遵子 羨

translations.literal: Zun's son Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, son of Zun.

sentences.zh: 羨爲離狐令。

translations.literal: Xian served as magistrate of Lihu.
translations.idiomatic: He Xian governed Lihu county.

sentences.zh: 既驕且吝，陵駕人物，鄕閭疾之如仇。

translations.literal: Proud yet miserly, he rode roughshod over people; his village detested him like an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant and stingy, he trampled neighbors who hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之末，何氏滅亡無遺焉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongjia era the He clan perished utterly with none surviving.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongjia catastrophe wiped out the He family line.

sentences.zh: 石苞

translations.literal: Shi Bao.
translations.idiomatic: General Shi Bao.

sentences.zh: 石苞，字仲容，渤海南皮人也。

translations.literal: Shi Bao, courtesy Zhongrong, was a man of Nanpi in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao from Nanpi in Bohai bore the courtesy name Zhongrong.

sentences.zh: 雅曠有智局，容儀偉麗，不修小節。

translations.literal: He was magnanimous and farseeing with strategic intelligence; his bearing was imposing and handsome; he did not fuss over minor points.
translations.idiomatic: Open-minded and sharp, striking in appearance, he spurned petty scruples.

sentences.zh: 故時人爲之語曰：「石仲容，姣無雙。

translations.literal: Therefore people of the time made a rhyme saying: Shi Zhongrong—beauty without peer.
translations.idiomatic: A ditty ran: Zhongrong's looks were unmatched.

sentences.zh: 」縣召爲吏，給農司馬。

translations.literal: The county summoned him clerk and assigned him aide to the agriculture marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The county drafted him as clerk serving the farming command.

sentences.zh: 會謁者陽翟郭玄信奉使，求人爲禦，司馬以苞及鄧艾給之。

translations.literal: It happened that herald Guo Xuanxin of Yangzhai was on mission seeking men as charioteers; the marshal supplied Bao along with Deng Ai.
translations.idiomatic: When envoy Guo Xuanxin needed drivers, the office lent Bao and Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 行十餘里，玄信謂二人曰：「子-{後}-並當至卿相。

translations.literal: After traveling over ten li Xuanxin told the two: You afterward will both reach minister rank.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-journey the envoy predicted both men would rise to chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 」苞曰：「禦隸也，何卿相乎？

translations.literal: Bao said: Charioteers are lackeys—how ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Bao scoffed that grooms could never become ministers.

sentences.zh: 」既而又被使到鄴，事久不決，乃販鐵-{於}-鄴市。

translations.literal: Later again dispatched to Ye, business dragged unresolved; therefore he peddled iron in the Ye market.
translations.idiomatic: A second Ye assignment stalled until he sold iron in the market.

sentences.zh: 市長沛國趙元儒名知人，見苞，異之，因與結交。

translations.literal: Market chief Zhao Yuanru of Pei, famed for judging men, saw Bao, marveled, and befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: Market inspector Zhao Yuanru spotted his promise and befriended him.

sentences.zh: 歎苞遠量，當至公輔，由是知名，見吏部郎許允，求爲小縣。

translations.literal: He praised Bao's long vision—that he would reach minister rank—whereby Bao became known; he visited Personnel Gentleman Xu Yun seeking a minor county.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's praise spread his name; Bao then asked Xu Yun for a small magistracy.

sentences.zh: 允謂苞曰：「卿是我輩人，當相引在朝廷，何欲小縣乎？

translations.literal: Yun told Bao: You are our sort of man; I shall pull you into court—why seek a petty county?
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun insisted court posts suited him better than a remote county.

sentences.zh: 」苞還歎息，不意允之知己乃如此也。

translations.literal: Bao returned sighing, not expecting Yun's recognition to run so deep.
translations.idiomatic: Bao marveled at such steadfast patronage.

sentences.zh: 稍遷景帝中護軍司馬。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted Marshal to the Central Army Protector under Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to marshal on Emperor Jing's guard staff.

sentences.zh: 宣帝聞苞好色薄行，以讓景帝。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan heard Bao chased women and behaved loosely and reproached Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi faulted his son for employing a libertine.

sentences.zh: 帝答曰：「苞雖細行不足，而有經國才略。

translations.literal: The emperor replied: Though Bao falls short in small conduct he possesses talent to order the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao replied that moral perfection rarely equals strategic genius.

sentences.zh: 夫貞廉之士，未必能經濟世務。

translations.literal: Upright and incorrupt men need not excel at managing worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Purists seldom master practical administration.

sentences.zh: 是以齊桓忘管仲之奢僭，而錄其匡合之大謀；

translations.literal: Therefore Duke Huan of Qi forgot Guan Zhong's extravagance and recorded his great plans that united the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Qi Huan overlooked Guan Zhong's excess for his statecraft.

sentences.zh: 漢高舍陳平之汙行，而取其六奇之妙算。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu set aside Chen Ping's stained reputation and took his six marvelous stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu ignored Chen Ping's morals for his stratagems.

sentences.zh: 苞雖未可以上儔二子，亦今日之選也。

translations.literal: Though Bao cannot quite rank with those two, he is still the choice for today.
translations.idiomatic: Bao fell short of those paragons yet remained the best available.

sentences.zh: 」意乃釋。

translations.literal: The concern then dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi relented.

sentences.zh: 徙鄴典農中郎將。

translations.literal: He was transferred Diannong Commandant at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He became Ye agriculture intendant.

sentences.zh: 時魏世王侯多居鄴下，尚書丁謐貴傾一時，並較時利。

translations.literal: At the time many Wei princes and marquises dwelt below Ye; Masters of Writing Ding Mi held sway and all competed for timely profit.
translations.idiomatic: Ye swarmed with nobles profiteering under Ding Mi's shadow.

sentences.zh: 苞奏列其事，由是益見稱。

translations.literal: Bao memorialized listing their deeds and thereby gained further praise.
translations.idiomatic: His expose of corruption won acclaim.

sentences.zh: 曆東萊、琅邪太守，所在皆有威惠。

translations.literal: He successively served Administrator of Donglai and Langya; wherever posted he combined awe and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect on the coast he balanced sternness and mercy.

sentences.zh: 遷徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Xuzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 文帝之敗-{於}-東關也，苞獨全軍而退。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was defeated at Dongguan, Bao alone brought his army back intact.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Zhao's Dongguan setback only Bao withdrew unscathed.

sentences.zh: 帝指所持節謂苞曰：「恨不以此授卿，以究大事。

translations.literal: The emperor pointed to the credential baton he held and told Bao: I regret not granting this to you to finish the great task.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao regretted not giving him supreme command.

sentences.zh: 」乃遷苞爲奮武將軍、假節、監青州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Therefore he promoted Bao General Who Rouses Might, with credential, supervising Qingzhou military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He named him general who rouses might over Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及諸葛誕舉兵淮南，苞統青州諸軍，督兗州刺史州泰、徐州刺史胡質，簡銳卒爲遊軍，以備外寇。

translations.literal: When Zhuge Dan raised troops in Huainan, Bao commanded Qingzhou forces, directing Yanzhou Inspector Zhou Tai and Xuzhou Inspector Hu Zhi, picking crack troops as mobile columns to guard against outside raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Against Zhuge Dan he coordinated Qing, Yan, and Xu columns with mobile elite guards.

sentences.zh: 呉遣大將朱異、丁奉等來迎，誕等留輜重-{於}-都陸，輕兵渡黎水。

translations.literal: Wu dispatched generals Zhu Yi and Ding Feng to meet them; Dan left baggage at Dulü and sent light troops across the Li River.
translations.idiomatic: Wu relief columns approached as Dan rushed light forces across the Li.

sentences.zh: 苞等逆擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Bao and allies attacked them head-on and smashed them.
translations.idiomatic: Bao struck first and shattered the relief army.

sentences.zh: 泰山太守胡烈以奇兵詭道襲都陸，盡焚其委輸。

translations.literal: Taishan Administrator Hu Lie took odd troops by hidden roads against Dulü and burned all supply convoys.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Lie raided Dulü supply lines by surprise.

sentences.zh: 異等收餘眾而退，壽春平。

translations.literal: Yi gathered surviving troops and withdrew; Shouchun was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi fled; Shouchun fell.

sentences.zh: 拜苞鎮東將軍，封東光侯、假節。

translations.literal: Bao was appointed General Who Guards the East, enfeoffed Marquis of Dongguang, with credential.
translations.idiomatic: He earned general who guards the east and the Dongguang marquisate.

sentences.zh: 頃之，代王基都督揚州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Shortly he replaced Wang Ji as Area Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded Wang Ji commanding Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 苞因入朝。

translations.literal: Bao therefore entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Court summons followed.

sentences.zh: 當還，辭高貴鄕公，留語盡日。

translations.literal: When due to return he took leave of Duke of Gaoguixiang and stayed talking the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Luoyang he spent the day with Cao Mao.

sentences.zh: 既出，白文帝曰：「非常主也。

translations.literal: After exiting he told Emperor Wen: That is no ordinary sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: He warned Sima Zhao that Cao Mao was extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 」數日而有成濟之事。

translations.literal: Within days came Cheng Ji's deed.
translations.idiomatic: Days later came Cheng Ji's regicide.

sentences.zh: -{後}-進位征東大將軍，俄遷驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Later he advanced to East-Conquering Grand General and soon moved to Cavalry-in-Chief General.
translations.idiomatic: Promotions stacked to east-conquering commander-in-chief then cavalry-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 文帝崩，賈充、荀勖議葬禮未定。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen died Jia Chong and Xun Xu debated burial rites unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao's death left funeral plans stalled between Jia Chong and Xun Xu.

sentences.zh: 苞時奔喪，慟哭曰：「基業如此，而以人臣終乎！

translations.literal: Bao then raced to mourning and wailed: An enterprise like this—to end as mere subject!
translations.idiomatic: Bao's keening insisted the regency deserved imperial burial.

sentences.zh: 」葬禮乃定。

translations.literal: Only then were funeral rites fixed.
translations.idiomatic: His protest settled the ceremony.

sentences.zh: -{後}-每與陳騫諷魏帝以歷數已終，天命有在。

translations.literal: Afterward he repeatedly joined Chen Qian hinting to the Wei emperor that the cosmic tally had ended and Heaven's Mandate rested elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Chen Qian urging abdication.

sentences.zh: 及禪位，苞有力焉。

translations.literal: When the abdication came Bao contributed force.
translations.idiomatic: He helped force the transfer.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，遷大司馬，進封樂陵郡公，加侍中，羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended he was promoted Grand Marshal, advanced Duke of Leling commandery, added Palace Attendant, feather-canopy bands and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi made him grand marshal, duke of Leling, with full honors.

sentences.zh: 自諸葛破滅，苞便鎮撫淮南，士馬強盛，邊境多務，苞既勤庶事，又以威德服物。

translations.literal: After Zhuge Dan's destruction Bao pacified Huainan; troops and horses were strong; the frontier was busy; Bao both toiled at myriad tasks and with awe and virtue won submission.
translations.idiomatic: He held Huainan with strong hosts, juggling logistics and moral sway.

sentences.zh: 淮北監軍王琛輕苞素微，又聞童謠曰：「宮中大馬-{幾}-作驢，大石壓之不得舒。

translations.literal: North-of-Huai supervisor Wang Chen despised Bao's humble origins and heard a children's rhyme: The great horse in the palace nearly turns donkey; a great stone presses it so it cannot stretch.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen mocked his birth and cited a rhyme hinting treason.

sentences.zh: 」因是密表苞與呉人交通。

translations.literal: Therefore he secretly memorialized that Bao communicated with Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen accused him of colluding with Wu.

sentences.zh: 先時望氣者云「東南有大兵起」。

translations.literal: Earlier qi-watchers had said: Great armies will arise in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Court astrologers had warned of southeastern war.

sentences.zh: 及琛表至，武帝甚疑之。

translations.literal: When Chen's memorial arrived Emperor Wu grew deeply suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew alarmed.

sentences.zh: 會荊州刺史胡烈表呉人欲大出爲寇，苞亦聞呉師將入，乃築壘遏水以自固。

translations.literal: It happened that Jing Inspector Hu Lie reported Wu planned a major raid; Bao too heard Wu armies would enter and therefore built ramparts blocking rivers to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Lie's alarm and Wu rumors drove Bao to fortify river lines.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，謂羊祜曰：「呉人每來，常東西相應，無緣偏爾，豈石苞果有不順乎？

translations.literal: The emperor heard and told Yang Hu: Whenever Wu men come they usually coordinate east and west—why only here—can Shi Bao truly harbor disloyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Wudi asked Yang Hu whether isolated alarms proved rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」祜深明之，而帝猶疑焉。

translations.literal: Hu clarified matters yet the emperor still doubted.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu eased concern only partly.

sentences.zh: 會苞子喬爲尚書郎，上召之，經日不至。

translations.literal: It happened Bao's son Qiao was Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; the emperor summoned him but for days he did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Son Qiao ignored repeated summons.

sentences.zh: 帝謂爲必叛，欲討苞而隱其事。

translations.literal: The emperor concluded rebellion certain and wished to attack Bao while concealing the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The throne planned secret punitive force.

sentences.zh: 遂下詔以苞不料賊勢，築壘遏水，勞擾百姓，策免其官。

translations.literal: Therefore an edict dismissed Bao for misjudging enemy strength, building ramparts and blocking rivers, vexing the people—stripping office by patent.
translations.idiomatic: A rescript cashiered him for panic defenses disturbing civilians.

sentences.zh: 遣太尉義陽王望率大軍征之，以備非常。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Prince Yiyang Sima Wang was dispatched leading a great army against him against emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Wang marched to hedge rebellion.

sentences.zh: 又敕鎮東將軍、琅邪王伷自下邳會壽春。

translations.literal: Also ordered General Who Guards the East, Prince of Langya Sima Zhou from Xiapi to converge on Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhou was to join from Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 苞用掾孫鑠計，放兵歩出，住都亭待罪。

translations.literal: Bao adopted clerk Sun Shuo's plan: release troops dismounted, exit on foot, halt at the metropolitan pavilion awaiting judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Following Sun Shuo he disarmed and waited at the capital lodge.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，意解。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, his mind eased.
translations.idiomatic: The gesture calmed the throne.

sentences.zh: 及苞詣闕，以公還第。

translations.literal: When Bao reached the palace gates he was sent home as duke.
translations.idiomatic: He entered brief audience then retired under ducal rank.

sentences.zh: 苞自恥受任無效而無怨色。

translations.literal: Bao himself felt shame at ineffectual mandate yet showed no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed himself without bitterness.

sentences.zh: 時鄴奚官督郭暠上書理苞。

translations.literal: At the time Ye eunuch superintendent Guo Hao submitted a memorial vindicating Bao.
translations.idiomatic: A Ye palace steward petitioned in his defense.

sentences.zh: 帝詔曰：「前大司馬苞忠允清亮，才經世務，幹用之績，所曆可紀。

translations.literal: An imperial edict stated: Former Grand Marshal Bao was loyal, trustworthy, clear, and bright; talent spanning worldly affairs; administrative merit recorded wherever he served.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi praised his past loyalty and competence.

sentences.zh: 宜掌教典，以贊時政。

translations.literal: He ought to oversee instructional norms and assist current governance.
translations.idiomatic: He should teach and advise policy.

sentences.zh: 其以苞爲司徒。

translations.literal: Let Bao be Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The court restored him as minister of education.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏：「苞前有折撓，不堪其任。

translations.literal: Authorities memorialized: Bao earlier suffered setback and cannot bear the charge;
translations.idiomatic: Officials argued his earlier failure disqualified him.

sentences.zh: 以公還第，已爲弘厚，不宜擢用。

translations.literal: Sending him home as duke already showed generosity—he should not be promoted.
translations.idiomatic: They said retiring him unpunished was mercy enough.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「呉人輕脆，終無能爲。

translations.literal: Closing their memorial an edict stated: Wu men are flighty and brittle and ultimately incapable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed their objection.

sentences.zh: 故疆埸之事，但欲完固守備，使不得越逸而已。

translations.literal: Therefore border affairs aim only to complete solid defense so they cannot slip past.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier policy required containment only.

sentences.zh: 以苞計畫不同，慮敵過甚，故征還更授。

translations.literal: Because Bao's plans differed and he overworried the foe he was recalled and reassigned.
translations.idiomatic: His caution prompted recall, not treason.

sentences.zh: 昔鄧禹撓-{於}-關中，而終輔漢室，豈以一眚而掩大德哉！

translations.literal: Formerly Deng Yu stumbled in Guanzhong yet ultimately aided Han—how for one slip obscure great virtue!
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yu's setback did not erase Han service.

sentences.zh: 」-{於}-是就位。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took office.
translations.idiomatic: Bao resumed the ministry.

sentences.zh: 苞奏：「州郡農桑未有賞罰之-{制}-，宜遣掾屬循行，皆當均其土宜，舉其殿最，然-{後}-黜陟焉。

translations.literal: Bao memorialized: Commanderies lack reward-and-punishment regulations for farming and sericulture; it is fitting to dispatch staff to tour, equalizing each soil's fitness, ranking best and worst, then demoting and promoting.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed agricultural inspectors ranking regional yields.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「農殖者，爲政之本，有國之大務也。

translations.literal: Closing his memorial an edict stated: Husbandry is the root of governance and the great task of possessing a state.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered that farming anchored rule.

sentences.zh: 雖欲安時興化，不先富而教之，其道無由。

translations.literal: Though wishing to pacify the age and raise transformation, unless first enriching then teaching them there is no way.
translations.idiomatic: Peace and moral instruction require prosperity first.

sentences.zh: 而至今四海多事，軍國用廣，加承征伐之-{後}-，屢有水旱之事，倉庫不充，百姓無積。

translations.literal: Yet now within the Four Seas troubles are many; army and state expenses are vast; added to successive campaigns there have been repeated floods and droughts; granaries are not full; commoners have no surplus.
translations.idiomatic: War and famine had emptied stores.

sentences.zh: 古道稼穡樹藝，司徒掌之。

translations.literal: By ancient ways sowing and planting fall under the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Classically the minister of education oversaw crops.

sentences.zh: 今雖登論道，然經國立政，惟時所急，故陶唐之世，稷官爲重。

translations.literal: Now though We ascend to discuss the Way, ordering the state and establishing government follows urgent seasons; hence in Tang Yao's age the grain officer weighed heaviest.
translations.idiomatic: Even sage kings prioritized agriculture.

sentences.zh: 今司徒位當其任，乃心王事，有毀家紓國，乾乾匪躬之志。

translations.literal: Now the Minister of Education holds that charge; let his heart be on royal affairs with resolve to ruin family to relieve state and toil tirelessly without self-regard.
translations.idiomatic: The edict demanded sacrificial zeal from Bao.

sentences.zh: 其使司徒督察州郡播殖，將委事任成，垂拱仰辦。

translations.literal: Let the Minister of Education supervise commanderies in planting; We shall delegate the task and achieve success with arms folded looking upward.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi tasked him with nationwide crop drives.

sentences.zh: 若宜有所循行者，其增置掾屬十人，聽取王官更練事業者。

translations.literal: If touring inspection should proceed add ten staff clerks drawn from seasoned royal officials.
translations.idiomatic: Up to ten deputy inspectors could come from veteran courtiers.

sentences.zh: 」苞在位稱爲忠勤，帝每委任焉。

translations.literal: Closing the edict: Bao while in office was praised as loyal and diligent, and the emperor repeatedly entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: After the long rescript closed, contemporaries still hailed his diligence and imperial trust.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: His death followed.

sentences.zh: 帝發哀-{於}-朝堂，賜秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，錢三十萬，布百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor expressed mourning in the court hall; granted secret burial vessels, one court robe, one suit of clothes, three hundred thousand cash, one hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning brought burial gifts matching prior magnates.

sentences.zh: 及葬，給節、幢、麾、曲蓋、追鋒車、鼓吹、介士、大車，皆如魏司空陳泰故事。

translations.literal: At burial were supplied baton, canopy banners, curved umbrella, hurrying-hearse carriage, bands, armored escort, and great carts—all per precedent of Wei Minister of Works Chen Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral pomp matched Chen Tai's Wei-era honors.

sentences.zh: 車駕臨送-{於}-東掖門外。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage escorted to outside the eastern Ye gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the cortège past the east portal.

sentences.zh: 策諡曰武。

translations.literal: By patent posthumous title Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He was canonized Wu.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，詔苞等並爲王功，列-{於}-銘饗。

translations.literal: Early in Xianning an edict grouped Bao among Wang-era merit ministers recorded for temple sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Xianning enrolled him among Jin founding peers honored at shrines.

sentences.zh: 苞豫爲《終-{制}-》曰：「延陵薄葬，孔子以爲達禮；

translations.literal: Bao beforehand wrote Final Burial Instructions stating: Yanling's thin burial Confucius deemed ritually enlightened;
translations.idiomatic: His testament cited Yanling's frugal tomb as sage-approved.

sentences.zh: 華元厚葬，《春秋》以爲不臣，古之明義也。

translations.literal: Hua Yuan's lavish burial the Spring and Autumn deemed unfilial to lord—such was ancient bright principle.
translations.idiomatic: It condemned Hua Yuan's excess as unministerial.

sentences.zh: 自今死亡者，皆斂以時服，不得兼重。

translations.literal: Henceforth the dead shall be dressed only in seasonal garments without doubling layers.
translations.idiomatic: He mandated simple shrouds.

sentences.zh: 又不得飯含，爲愚俗所爲。

translations.literal: Also no grain-in-mouth jade pearl—what vulgar folly practices.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade mouth pearls.

sentences.zh: 又不得設床帳明器也。

translations.literal: Also no bed curtains or mingqi grave goods.
translations.idiomatic: He banned tomb furnishings and figurines.

sentences.zh: 定窆之-{後}-，復土滿坎，一不得起墳種樹。

translations.literal: After fixing the grave and lowering the coffin, backfill the pit level—never mound earth or plant trees.
translations.idiomatic: He demanded flat graves without mounds or trees.

sentences.zh: 昔王孫裸葬矯時，其子奉命，君子不譏，況-{於}-合禮典者耶？

translations.literal: Formerly Yang Wangsun's naked burial corrected his age; his son obeyed; gentlemen did not mock—how much more when conforming to ritual canon?
translations.idiomatic: He invoked Yang Wangsun's austere burial as respectable.

sentences.zh: 」諸子皆奉遵遺令，又斷親戚故吏設祭。

translations.literal: His sons all obeyed the dying commands and further cut offerings from kin and former subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Heirs honored the will and refused condolence sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 有六子：越、喬、統、浚、俊、崇。

translations.literal: He had six sons: Yue, Qiao, Tong, Jun who bore courtesy name Jinglun, Jun who bore courtesy name Yanlun, and Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Six sons survived him: Yue, Qiao, Tong, two different men both romanized Jun distinguished by the courtesy names Jinglun and Yanlun, and Chong.

sentences.zh: 以統爲嗣。

translations.literal: Tong was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: The primary heir was Tong.

sentences.zh: =苞子 統=

translations.literal: The manuscript line reads equals Bao's son Tong equals.
translations.idiomatic: Heading marker for Tong, son of Shi Bao.

sentences.zh: 統字弘緒，歷位射聲校尉、大鴻臚。

translations.literal: Tong, courtesy Hongxu, successively held posts as Commandant of Archers Who Shoot at Sound and Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tong rose through commandant of sound-archers to grand herald.

sentences.zh: 子順，爲尚書郎。

translations.literal: Son Shun became Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shun served at the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: =苞子 越=

translations.literal: The manuscript line reads equals Bao's son Yue equals.
translations.idiomatic: Heading marker for Yue, son of Shi Bao.

sentences.zh: 越字弘倫，早卒。

translations.literal: Yue, courtesy Honglun, died young.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yue died in youth.

sentences.zh: =苞子 喬=

translations.literal: The manuscript line reads equals Bao's son Qiao equals.
translations.idiomatic: Heading marker for Qiao, son of Shi Bao.

sentences.zh: 喬字弘祖，曆尚書郎、散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Qiao, courtesy Hongzu, successively served Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and Gentleman Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Qiao held ministry and cavalier posts.

sentences.zh: 帝既召喬不得，深疑苞反。

translations.literal: Because when the emperor summoned Qiao he did not appear, the throne deeply suspected Bao of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao's failure to answer summons fed rumors of Bao's treason.

sentences.zh: 及苞至，有慚色，謂之曰「卿子-{幾}-破卿門」。

translations.literal: When Bao arrived the emperor showed shame and told him: Your son nearly destroyed your house.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan apologized yet blamed Qiao for nearly ruining the clan.

sentences.zh: 苞遂廢之，終身不聽仕。

translations.literal: Bao therefore cast Qiao aside and to the end of life refused to let him take office.
translations.idiomatic: Bao disowned him from official careers forever.

sentences.zh: 又以有穢行，徙頓丘，與弟崇同被害。

translations.literal: Also because of scandalous conduct he was banished to Dunqiu and together with younger brother Chong suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Later disgrace sent him to Dunqiu where he and Chong were killed.

sentences.zh: 二子超、熙亡走得免。

translations.literal: Two sons Chao and Xi fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Chao and Xi ran away and survived.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎之起義也，以超爲折-{衝}-將軍，討孫秀，以功封侯。

translations.literal: When Prince Chengdu of Chengdu Sima Ying raised loyal troops he appointed Chao General Who Breaks the Charge to campaign against Sun Xiu and for merit was enfeoffed marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying named Chao van leader against Sun Xiu, earning a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 又爲振武將軍，征荊州賊李辰。

translations.literal: Again he was General Who Rouses Might and campaigned against Jing bandit Li Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He next suppressed bandit Li Chen in Jing.

sentences.zh: 穎與長沙王乂相攻，超常爲前鋒，遷中護軍。

translations.literal: When Ying and Prince Changsha Sima Yi attacked each other Chao often served as vanguard and was promoted Central Army Protector.
translations.idiomatic: In civil war between Ying and Yi he led van guards.

sentences.zh: 陳昣等挾惠帝北伐，超走還鄴。

translations.literal: When Chen Zhen and others forced Emperor Hui north Chao fled back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: During the forced northern expedition Chao bolted to Ye.

sentences.zh: 穎使超距帝-{於}-蕩陰，王師敗績，超逼帝幸鄴宮。

translations.literal: Ying ordered Chao to block the emperor at Tangyin; imperial troops were routed; Chao pressed the emperor to go to the Ye palace.
translations.idiomatic: At Tangyin Chao drove imperial guards aside and escorted the emperor to Ye.

sentences.zh: 會王浚攻穎-{於}-鄴，穎以超爲右將軍以距浚，大敗而歸。

translations.literal: When Sima Jun attacked Ying at Ye, Ying made Chao right general to oppose Jun and returned in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: A relief bid against Sima Jun collapsed.

sentences.zh: 從駕之洛陽，西遷長安。

translations.literal: Following the entourage to Luoyang he moved west to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He then trailed the court westward.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒以超領北中郎將，使與穎共距東海王越。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Sima Yong put Chao in charge as North Central General-in-Chief ordering him with Ying to resist Prince of Donghai Sima Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong teamed him with Ying against Sima Yue.

sentences.zh: 超-{於}-滎陽募兵，右將軍王闡與典兵中郎趙則並受超節度，爲豫州刺史劉喬繼援。

translations.literal: Chao recruited troops at Xingyang; Right General Wang Chan and Dian-bing Commandant Zhao Ze both took his orders as reinforcements for Yuzhou Inspector Liu Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He levied men at Xingyang under Liu Qiao's relief column.

sentences.zh: 范陽王虓逆擊斬超，而熙得走免。

translations.literal: Prince of Fanyang Sima Xiao counterattacked, beheaded Chao, while Xi got away.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiao killed Chao; Xi escaped.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，爲太傅越參軍。

translations.literal: During Yongjia he was aide to Grand Tutor Sima Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongjia he joined Sima Yue's staff.

sentences.zh: =苞子 浚=

translations.literal: The manuscript line reads equals Bao's son Jun courtesy Jinglun equals.
translations.idiomatic: Heading marker for Shi Jun the elder, courtesy Jinglun.

sentences.zh: 浚字景倫，清儉有鑒識，敬愛人物。

translations.literal: Jun, courtesy Jinglun, was clear, frugal, and discerning, respectful and cherishing worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jun was austere, perceptive, and principled.

sentences.zh: 位至黃門侍郎，爲當世名士，早卒。

translations.literal: He rose to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates and was a celebrated gentleman of the age; he died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young yet famed as a yellow-gate moral exemplar.

sentences.zh: =苞子 俊=

translations.literal: The manuscript line reads equals Bao's son Jun courtesy Yanlun equals.
translations.idiomatic: Heading marker for Shi Jun the younger, courtesy Yanlun.

sentences.zh: 俊字彥倫，少有名譽，議者稱爲令器。

translations.literal: Jun, courtesy Yanlun, had reputation in youth; critics called him fine timber.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jun the younger, styled Yanlun, was hailed as promising talent.

sentences.zh: 官至陽平太守，早卒。

translations.literal: His office reached Administrator of Yangping; he died young.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Yangping briefly before early death.

sentences.zh: =苞子 崇=

translations.literal: The manuscript line reads equals Bao's son Chong equals.
translations.idiomatic: Heading marker for Chong, son of Shi Bao.

sentences.zh: 崇字季倫，生-{於}-青州，故小名齊奴。

translations.literal: Chong, courtesy Jilun, was born in Qingzhou, hence childhood name Qinu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong, nicknamed Qinu, was Qingzhou-born.

sentences.zh: 少敏惠，勇而有謀。

translations.literal: In youth he was keen and clever, brave yet calculating.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and bold, he showed strategic nerve early.

sentences.zh: 苞臨終，分財物與諸子，獨不及崇。

translations.literal: When Bao faced death he divided property among sons but left out Chong alone.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Bao skipped Chong in the division.

sentences.zh: 其母以爲言，苞曰：「此兒雖小，-{後}-自能得。

translations.literal: His mother raised the matter; Bao said: Though this child is small, afterward he will gain wealth on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Bao told her the boy would enrich himself later.

sentences.zh: 」年二十餘，爲修武令，有能名。

translations.literal: At over twenty he became magistrate of Xiuwu with a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He proved an able Xiuwu magistrate.

sentences.zh: 入爲散騎郎，遷城陽太守。

translations.literal: He entered as Cavalier Gentleman and was promoted Administrator of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Court duty led to Chengyang prefect.

sentences.zh: 伐呉有功，封安陽鄕侯。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Wu he earned merit and was enfeoffed Village Marquis of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Conquest of Wu won him the Anyang village marquisate.

sentences.zh: 在郡雖有職務，好學不倦，以疾自解。

translations.literal: Though burdened with prefect duties he loved study tirelessly and resigned citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: He quit office claiming illness to keep reading.

sentences.zh: 頃之，拜黃門郎。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned as yellow-gate gentleman.

sentences.zh: 兄統忤扶風王駿，有司承旨奏統，將加重罰，既而見原。

translations.literal: Elder brother Tong offended Prince of Fufeng Sima Jun; authorities carrying out intent memorialized Tong for heavy punishment, yet he was later forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Tong clashed with Sima Jun and barely escaped harsh sentence.

sentences.zh: 以崇不詣闕謝恩，有司欲復加統罪。

translations.literal: Because Chong did not go to court to thank for grace authorities wished again to add Tong's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's failure to present thanks threatened renewed charges against Tong.

sentences.zh: 崇自表曰：「臣兄統以先父之恩，早被優遇，出入清顯，歷位盡勤。

translations.literal: Chong personally memorialized: Your servant's elder brother Tong, thanks to late father's favor, long enjoyed generous treatment, moving among pure offices and serving diligently.
translations.idiomatic: Chong petitioned for Tong, citing dutiful service.

sentences.zh: 伏度聖心，有以垂察。

translations.literal: Your servant measures that sage mind must already perceive this.
translations.idiomatic: He appealed to imperial discernment.

sentences.zh: 近爲扶風王駿橫所誣謗，司隸中丞等飛筆重奏，劾案深文，累塵天聽。

translations.literal: Recently Prince of Fufeng Sima Jun slandered him wantonly; metropolitan commandant and palace assistant censors flew pens with severe memorials, exhausting heavenly hearing.
translations.idiomatic: He accused Jun of orchestrated slander.

sentences.zh: 臣兄弟跼蹐，憂心如悸。

translations.literal: Your servant's brothers stand on tiptoes in fear; worry grips the heart like pounding.
translations.idiomatic: He described family terror.

sentences.zh: 駿戚屬尊重，權要赫奕。

translations.literal: Jun's kin are lofty; his power blazes.
translations.idiomatic: He stressed Jun's intimidating clan.

sentences.zh: 內外有司，望風承旨。

translations.literal: Within and without offices sniff the wind and carry out intent.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaucrats rushed to obey Jun.

sentences.zh: 苟有所惡，易-{於}-投卵。

translations.literal: If they harbor hatred it is easier than smashing an egg.
translations.idiomatic: Malice could crush them effortlessly.

sentences.zh: 自統枉劾以來，臣兄弟不敢一言稍自申理。

translations.literal: Since Tong's wrongful impeachment your servant's brothers have not dared one word to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tong's frame-up they had stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 戢舌鉗口，惟須刑書。

translations.literal: They folded tongues and clamped mouths awaiting only the sentencing document.
translations.idiomatic: They waited mute for punishment.

sentences.zh: 古人稱「榮華-{於}-順旨，枯槁-{於}-逆違」，誠哉斯言，-{於}-今信矣。

translations.literal: The ancients said glory follows compliant intent and withering follows opposition—true words; believed today.
translations.idiomatic: He cited proverb on favor currying versus ruin.

sentences.zh: 是以雖董司直繩，不能不深其文，抱枉含謗，不得不輸其理。

translations.literal: Therefore though investigating officers hold straight rope they cannot but deepen the wording; bearing wrong and bearing slander they cannot but lay out the reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Even honest judges bow to pressure.

sentences.zh: 幸賴陛下天聽四達，靈鑒昭遠，存先父勳德之重，察臣等勉勵之志。

translations.literal: Fortunately leaning on Your Majesty's hearing reaching four quarters and spirit mirror shining far, cherishing late father's merit and observing our striving will.
translations.idiomatic: He praised the emperor's fairness.

sentences.zh: 中詔申料，罪譴澄雪。

translations.literal: Inner edicts reviewed and guilt's snow cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial review absolved them.

sentences.zh: 臣等刻肌碎首，未足上報。

translations.literal: Your servants would carve flesh and shatter heads yet cannot repay above.
translations.idiomatic: He vowed gratitude beyond repayment.

sentences.zh: 臣即以今月十四日，與兄統、浚等詣公車門拜表謝恩。

translations.literal: Your servant on the fourteenth of this month with elder brothers Tong and Jun went to the Public Coach Gate with memorial thanking grace.
translations.idiomatic: They thanked at the proper gate.

sentences.zh: 伏度奏禦之日，暫經天聽。

translations.literal: Your servant measures that when the memorial reached the throne it briefly passed heavenly hearing.
translations.idiomatic: He assumed brief imperial notice.

sentences.zh: 此月二十日，忽被蘭台禁止符，以統蒙宥，恩出非常，臣晏然私門，曾不陳謝，復見彈奏，訕辱理盡。

translations.literal: On the twentieth this month we suddenly received Orchid Terrace prohibition talismans: because Tong received mercy beyond ordinary your servant stayed calmly at private gate without presenting thanks; again came impeachment claiming shameless neglect.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaucrats attacked them for tardy thanks.

sentences.zh: 臣始聞此，惶懼狼狽，靜而思之，固無怪也。

translations.literal: Your servant first hearing this was panic-stricken; reflecting quietly it is no wonder.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned understanding of court politics.

sentences.zh: 苟尊勢所驅，何所不至，望奉法之直繩，不可得也。

translations.literal: Where awesome power drives what limit exists; hoping for straight rope of law is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Power brokers warp justice.

sentences.zh: 臣以凡才，累荷顯重，不能負載析薪，以答萬分。

translations.literal: Your servant with ordinary talent has repeatedly borne honor yet cannot split firewood to repay the myriad fraction.
translations.idiomatic: He confessed humble inability.

sentences.zh: 一月之中，奏劾頻加，曲之與直，非臣所計。

translations.literal: Within one month impeachments piled; crooked versus straight is not for your servant to reckon.
translations.idiomatic: Serial charges overwhelmed them.

sentences.zh: 所愧不能承奉戚屬，自陷-{於}-此。

translations.literal: What shames is inability to flatter powerful kin and thus falling into this.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed refusal to court Jun.

sentences.zh: 不媚-{於}-灶，實愧王孫，《隨巢子》稱「明君之德，察情爲上，察事次之」。

translations.literal: Not flattering the kitchen god truly shames Yang Wangsun; the Suichaozi states: An enlightened lord's virtue examines feeling first, affairs second.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Suichaozi on discerning rulers.

sentences.zh: 所懷具經聖聽，伏待罪黜，無所多言。

translations.literal: What your servant harbors has reached sage hearing; awaiting dismissal nothing more need be said.
translations.idiomatic: He awaited punishment silently.

sentences.zh: 」由是事解。

translations.literal: Closing memorial the affair resolved.
translations.idiomatic: The petition cleared the crisis.

sentences.zh: 累遷散騎常侍、侍中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to senior attendant posts.

sentences.zh: 武帝以崇功臣子，有幹局，深器重之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu because Chong was a merit minister's son with administrative grasp deeply esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi favored him as capable noble heir.

sentences.zh: 元康初，楊駿輔政，大開封賞，多樹黨援。

translations.literal: Early in Yuankang Yang Jun assisted government and lavishly opened enfeoffments and rewards, planting party ties.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun's regency showered patronage.

sentences.zh: 崇與散騎郎蜀郡何攀共立議，奏-{於}-惠帝曰：「陛下聖德光被，皇靈啟祚，正位東宮，二十餘年，道化宣流，萬國歸心。

translations.literal: Chong together with Cavalier Gentleman He Pan of Shu jointly drafted advice memorializing Emperor Hui: Your Majesty's sagely virtue shines; imperial spirit opened fortune; correct position Eastern Palace over twenty years; transforming teaching spread; myriad regions turned hearts.
translations.idiomatic: They opened a paired memorial with ritual praise.

sentences.zh: 今承洪基，此乃天授。

translations.literal: Now inheriting great foundation—this is Heaven's grant.
translations.idiomatic: They hailed peaceful succession.

sentences.zh: 至-{於}-班賞行爵，優-{於}-泰始革命之初。

translations.literal: Yet granting ranks and rewards exceeds the liberality at Taishi founding revolution.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked excessive grants—first objection.

sentences.zh: 不安一也。

translations.literal: That is unease one.
translations.idiomatic: First warning against Yang Jun's gifts.

sentences.zh: 呉會僭逆，-{幾}--{於}-百年，邊境被其荼毒，朝廷爲之旰食。

translations.literal: Wu domain's usurpation and rebellion lasted nearly a century; borders suffered its poison; the court skipped meals over it.
translations.idiomatic: Second point: Wu had long vexed the realm.

sentences.zh: 先帝決獨斷之聰，奮神武之略，蕩滅逋寇，易-{於}-摧枯。

translations.literal: The late emperor with decisive wisdom and divine martial planning swept away fleeing bandits easier than snapping dry wood.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi crushed Wu decisively.

sentences.zh: 然謀臣猛將，猶有致思竭力之效。

translations.literal: Yet planning ministers and fierce generals still showed utmost loyal effort.
translations.idiomatic: Merit ministers earned their rewards.

sentences.zh: 而今恩澤之封，優-{於}-滅呉之功。

translations.literal: Now favor's overflow exceeds rewards for destroying Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun's gifts outstripped Wu conquerors—second unease.

sentences.zh: 不安二也。

translations.literal: That is unease two.
translations.idiomatic: Second objection stated.

sentences.zh: 上天眷祐，實在大晉，卜世之數，未知其紀。

translations.literal: Heaven's favor rests truly on Great Jin; numbered generations are not yet known.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's mandate should be husbanded.

translations.literal: Today's opening regulations must reach down to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent binds future ages.

sentences.zh: 若尊卑無差，有爵必進，數世之-{後}-，莫非公侯。

translations.literal: If high and low lack distinction and every holder of rank advances, after several generations none will not be duke or marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Rank inflation would nobble everyone—third unease.

sentences.zh: 不安三也。

translations.literal: That is unease three.
translations.idiomatic: Third objection stated.

sentences.zh: 臣等敢冒陳聞。

translations.literal: Your servants dare risk reporting.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted boldly.

sentences.zh: 竊謂泰始之初，及平呉論功，-{制}-度名牒，皆悉具存。

translations.literal: Your servants humbly think Taishi beginning and post-Wu merit discussions—institutions and name registers—all remain intact.
translations.idiomatic: Archives held fair precedents.

sentences.zh: 縱不能遠遵古典，尚當依准舊事。

translations.literal: Even if unable to follow remote antiquity still ought to align with old affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They urged matching earlier tables.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，弗納。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Hui ignored the protest.

sentences.zh: 出爲南中郎將、荊州刺史，領南蠻校尉，加鷹揚將軍。

translations.literal: He went out South Central General-in-Chief, Inspector of Jingzhou, heading Southern Man commandant, added General Who Displays Might.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jingzhou with frontier generalships.

sentences.zh: 崇在南中，得鴆鳥雛，以與-{後}-軍將軍王愷。

translations.literal: In southern lands Chong obtained zhen chick and gave it to Rear Army General Wang Kai.
translations.idiomatic: He shipped a forbidden zhen fledgling to Wang Kai.

sentences.zh: 時-{制}-，鴆鳥不得過江，爲司隸校尉傅祗所糾，詔原之，燒鴆-{於}-都街。

translations.literal: Current regulations forbid zhen birds crossing the river; Metropolitan Commandant Fu Di impeached him; an edict pardoned him and burned the bird in the capital street.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Di seized the bird; court burned it publicly.

sentences.zh: 崇穎悟有才氣，而任俠無行檢。

translations.literal: Chong was bright and talented yet acted the knight-errant without moral restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant but unscrupulous.

sentences.zh: 在荊州，劫遠使商客，致富不貲。

translations.literal: In Jingzhou he robbed distant envoys and merchants, growing rich beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: He plundered traders for fortune.

sentences.zh: 徵爲大司農，以征書未至擅去官免。

translations.literal: Summoned Grand Minister of Agriculture he was dismissed for quitting office before summons arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He lost grand agrarian post for premature resignation.

sentences.zh: 頃之，拜太僕，出爲征虜將軍，假節、監徐州諸軍事，鎮下邳。

translations.literal: Shortly appointed Grand Coachman he went out General Who Subdues Captives, with credential, supervising Xuzhou military affairs, headquartered at Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as coachman then Xuzhou commander.

sentences.zh: 崇有別館在河陽之金-{谷}-，一名梓澤，送者傾都，帳飲-{於}-此焉。

translations.literal: Chong had a villa at Golden Valley in Heyang, also called Zize; send-offs filled the capital; tent feasts were held here.
translations.idiomatic: His Golden Valley estate hosted famous farewell parties.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，與徐州刺史高誕爭酒相侮，爲軍司所奏，免官。

translations.literal: Arriving on station he quarreled over wine insultingly with Xuzhou Inspector Gao Dan; army clerk memorialized; he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: A drunken insult duel with Gao Dan cost his job.

sentences.zh: 復拜衞尉，與潘岳諂事賈謐。

translations.literal: Reappointed Guards Commandant he toadied to Jia Mi with Pan Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He curried Jia Mi beside Pan Yue.

sentences.zh: 謐與之親善，號曰「二十四友」。

translations.literal: Mi treated him intimately, dubbing them the Twenty-Four Friends.
translations.idiomatic: They joined Mi's literary cabal.

sentences.zh: 廣城君每出，崇降車路左，望塵而拜，其卑佞如此。

translations.literal: Whenever Lady Guangcheng emerged Chong descended his carriage on the road's left, bowing to dust—his servility ran so low.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed to Jia Nanfeng's mother in the dirt.

sentences.zh: 財產豐積，室宇宏麗。

translations.literal: His wealth piled high and his halls were vast and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunes and mansions swelled beyond measure.

sentences.zh: -{後}-房百數，皆曳紈繡，珥金翠。

translations.literal: Behind chambers numbered in hundreds; all trailed fine silk and wore gold and kingfisher ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Concubines beyond count wore brocade and jade.

sentences.zh: 絲竹盡當時之選，庖膳窮水陸之珍。

translations.literal: Music drew the day's finest performers; kitchens exhausted delicacies of land and sea.
translations.idiomatic: Orchestras and banquets pushed every culinary extreme.

sentences.zh: 與貴戚王愷、羊琇之徒以奢靡相尚。

translations.literal: With noble in-laws Wang Kai and Yang Xiu and their ilk he vied in extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: He raced Wang Kai and Yang Xiu in conspicuous waste.

sentences.zh: 愷以𥹋澳釜，崇以蠟代薪。

translations.literal: Kai washed cauldrons with rice rinse; Chong burned candle wax for firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai scoured pots with grain rinse while Chong lit fires with beeswax.

sentences.zh: 愷作紫絲布歩障四十里，崇作錦歩障五十里以敵之。

translations.literal: Kai raised forty li of purple silk screens; Chong answered with fifty li of brocade screens.
translations.idiomatic: Forty li of violet barriers faced fifty li of embroidered drapes.

sentences.zh: 崇塗屋以椒，愷用赤石脂。

translations.literal: Chong plastered rooms with peppercorn plaster; Kai used red ochre clay.
translations.idiomatic: Pepper-infused plaster met cinnabar-coated walls.

sentences.zh: 崇、愷爭豪如此。

translations.literal: Thus Chong and Kai competed in arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Their rivalry defined Jin decadence.

sentences.zh: 武帝每助愷，嘗以珊瑚樹賜之，高二尺許，枝柯扶疏，世所罕比。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu usually aided Kai; once he gifted a coral tree over two chi tall, branching luxuriantly, rarely matched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored Kai with a tall coral centerpiece.

sentences.zh: 愷以示崇，崇便以鐵如意擊之，應手而碎。

translations.literal: Kai showed it to Chong; Chong struck it with an iron ruyi-scepter and it shattered at the blow.
translations.idiomatic: Chong smashed the coral with a metal wand.

sentences.zh: 愷既惋惜，又以爲嫉己之寶，聲色方厲。

translations.literal: Kai lamented and thought Chong jealous of his treasure; his voice grew fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Kai raged at the insult.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「不足多恨，今還卿。

translations.literal: Chong said: Not worth much regret—now I repay you.
translations.idiomatic: Chong shrugged off the loss.

sentences.zh: 」乃命左右悉取珊瑚樹，有高三四尺者六七株，條幹絶俗，光彩曜日，如愷比者甚眾。

translations.literal: He ordered attendants fetch coral trees; six or seven stood three or four chi tall, stems surpassing custom, brilliance dazzling the sun—many matched Kai's.
translations.idiomatic: He unveiled a warehouse of loftier corals.

sentences.zh: 愷忄兄然自失矣。

translations.literal: Kai stood dazed and defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai slumped, utterly outspent.

sentences.zh: 崇爲客作豆粥，咄嗟便辦。

translations.literal: When entertaining guests Chong prepared bean gruel ready in a shout.
translations.idiomatic: Bean porridge appeared on command.

sentences.zh: 每冬，得韭萍齏。

translations.literal: Each winter he obtained leek-and-water-shield relish.
translations.idiomatic: Winter brought faux spring leek relish.

sentences.zh: 嘗與愷出遊，爭入洛城，崇牛迅若飛禽，愷絶不能及。

translations.literal: Once traveling with Kai they raced into Luoyang; Chong's ox ran swift as fowl and Kai could not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: His cattle outran Kai's carriage into the capital.

sentences.zh: 愷每以此三事爲根，乃密貨崇帳下問其所以。

translations.literal: Kai took these three feats as grievances and secretly bribed Chong's tent staff asking how.
translations.idiomatic: Kai bought Chong's servants for trade secrets.

sentences.zh: 答云：「豆至難煮，豫作熟末，客來，但作白粥以投之耳。

translations.literal: They answered: Beans are hard to boil—pre-roast flour powder; when guests come pour into white gruel.
translations.idiomatic: They revealed pre-cooked bean flour trick.

sentences.zh: 韭萍齏是搗韭根雜以麥苗耳。

translations.literal: The leek relish is pounded leek roots mixed with wheat sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: Relish was leek roots with cereal shoots.

sentences.zh: 牛奔不遲，良由馭者逐不及反-{制}-之，可聽蹁轅則駃矣。

translations.literal: The ox runs fast because drivers cannot reverse reins in time—let shafts sway freely and it gallops.
translations.idiomatic: Loose traces made oxen sprint.

sentences.zh: 」-{於}-是悉從之，遂爭長焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kai copied all and finally matched him.
translations.idiomatic: Kai mimicked every gimmick.

sentences.zh: 崇-{後}-知之，因殺所告者。

translations.literal: Later Chong learned and killed the informants.
translations.idiomatic: Chong murdered the stool-pigeons.

sentences.zh: 嘗與王敦入太學，見顏回、原憲之象，顧而歎曰：「若與之同升孔堂，去人何必有間。

translations.literal: Once entering the Imperial Academy with Wang Dun he saw statues of Yan Hui and Yuan Xian; turning he sighed: Had I ascended Confucius's hall with them, what gap need separate us from others?
translations.idiomatic: At Confucius Temple he envied Yan Hui's poverty sages.

sentences.zh: 」敦曰：「不知餘人云何，子貢去卿差近。

translations.literal: Dun said: I know not others—Zi Gong fell somewhat short of you.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun teased him as closer to Zigong.

sentences.zh: 」崇正色曰：「士當身名俱泰，何至甕牖哉！

translations.literal: Chong replied sternly: A gentleman should possess body and fame alike in prosperity—why lodge in a jar window?
translations.idiomatic: He disdained humble poverty.

sentences.zh: 」其立意類此。

translations.literal: His attitudes were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Such vanity colored his whole ethic.

sentences.zh: 劉輿兄弟少時爲王愷所嫉，愷召之宿，因欲坑之。

translations.literal: In youth brothers Liu Yu were envied by Wang Kai; Kai summoned them overnight intending to bury them alive.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai tried to murder the Liu brothers.

sentences.zh: 崇素與輿等善，聞當有變，夜馳詣愷，問二劉所在，愷迫卒不得隱。

translations.literal: Chong was always friendly with Yu; hearing trouble brewed he rode by night to Kai demanding where the two Liu were; Kai pressed could not hide.
translations.idiomatic: Chong rushed to rescue them.

sentences.zh: 崇徑進-{於}--{後}-齋索出，同車而去。

translations.literal: Chong went straight to rear chambers and pulled them out, riding away together in one carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He dragged them from back rooms and fled.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「年少何以輕就人宿！

translations.literal: He told them: Youth—why lightly lodge overnight with others!
translations.idiomatic: He scolded their naivete.

sentences.zh: 」輿深德之。

translations.literal: Yu deeply thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu owed him his life.

sentences.zh: 及賈謐誅，崇以黨與免官。

translations.literal: When Jia Mi was executed Chong was cashiered as partisan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi's fall ended Chong's office.

sentences.zh: 時趙王倫專權，崇甥歐陽建與倫有隙。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Zhao of Zhao Sima Lun monopolized power; Chong's nephew Ouyang Jian bore grudge against Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun feuded with nephew Ouyang Jian.

sentences.zh: 崇有妓曰綠珠，美而豔，善吹笛。

translations.literal: Chong kept a singing girl Green Pearl, lovely and radiant, skilled on flute.
translations.idiomatic: His famed concubine Green Pearl played flute.

sentences.zh: 孫秀使人求之。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu sent men demanding her.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu coveted Green Pearl.

sentences.zh: 崇時在金-{谷}-別館，方登涼臺，臨清流，婦人侍側。

translations.literal: Chong was then at Golden Valley villa, mounting a cool terrace overlooking clear stream with women attending.
translations.idiomatic: He lounged at Golden Valley estate.

sentences.zh: 使者以告。

translations.literal: Envoys reported the demand.
translations.idiomatic: Messengers tracked him down.

sentences.zh: 崇盡出其婢妾數十人以示之，皆蘊蘭麝，被羅縠，曰：「在所擇。

translations.literal: Chong brought forth dozens of maids and concubines all scented with musk clad in gauze saying: Choose whom you will.
translations.idiomatic: He offered substitute beauties.

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「君侯服御麗則麗矣，然本受命指索綠珠，不識孰是？

translations.literal: Envoy said: Lord's attendants are splendid indeed, yet orders aim at Green Pearl—which is she?
translations.idiomatic: They insisted on Green Pearl.

sentences.zh: 」崇勃然曰：「綠珠吾所愛，不可得也。

translations.literal: Chong flared: Green Pearl is my beloved—not obtainable.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「君侯博古通今，察遠照邇，願加三思。

translations.literal: Envoy said: Lord reads antiquity through today; examine far and near—think thrice.
translations.idiomatic: They threatened consequences.

sentences.zh: 」崇曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Chong said: No.
translations.idiomatic: He held firm.

sentences.zh: 」使者出而又反，崇竟不許。

translations.literal: Envoy left and returned; Chong still refused.
translations.idiomatic: Second embassy failed.

sentences.zh: 秀怒，乃勸倫誅崇、建。

translations.literal: Xiu raged and urged Lun to execute Chong and Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu pushed execution.

sentences.zh: 崇、建亦潛知其計，乃與黃門郎潘岳陰勸淮南王允、齊王冏以圖倫、秀。

translations.literal: Chong and Jian secretly learned the plot and with Gentleman at Yellow Gates Pan Yue secretly urged Prince Huainan Sima Yun and Prince Qi Sima Jiong against Lun and Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: They plotted counter-coup with Pan Yue.

sentences.zh: 秀覺之，遂矯詔收崇及潘岳、歐陽建等。

translations.literal: Xiu detected it and forged edict arresting Chong, Pan Yue, Ouyang Jian and others.
translations.idiomatic: Forged warrants seized the circle.

sentences.zh: 崇正宴-{於}-樓上，介士到門。

translations.literal: Chong feasted upstairs when armored guards reached the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers interrupted his banquet.

sentences.zh: 崇謂綠珠曰：「我今爲爾得罪。

translations.literal: Chong told Green Pearl: Today I suffer offense for your sake.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed her charm.

sentences.zh: 」綠珠泣曰：「當效死-{於}-官前。

translations.literal: Green Pearl wept: I shall die before officers.
translations.idiomatic: She vowed martyrdom.

sentences.zh: 」因自投-{於}-樓下而死。

translations.literal: She threw herself from the tower and died.
translations.idiomatic: She leaped to her death.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「吾不過流徙交、廣耳。

translations.literal: Chong said: I shall only be exiled to Jiao or Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He expected mere banishment.
