sentences.zh: 」及車載詣東市，崇乃歎曰：「奴輩利吾家財。

translations.literal: When cart bore him to eastern market he sighed: Slaves covet my household wealth.
translations.idiomatic: At execution he cursed greedy servants.

sentences.zh: 」收者答曰：「知財致害，何不早散之？

translations.literal: Arresting officer replied: Knowing wealth brings harm why not distribute early?
translations.idiomatic: Guards mocked his hoarding.

sentences.zh: 」崇不能答。

translations.literal: Chong could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: He had no reply.

sentences.zh: 崇母兄妻子無少長皆被害，死者十五人，崇時年五十二。

translations.literal: Chong's mother, elder brothers, wives, children—all ages none spared—fifteen died; Chong was fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen kin perished; Chong died at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 初，崇家稻米飯在地，經宿皆化爲螺，時人以爲族滅之應。

translations.literal: Earlier Chong household rice steamed on ground overnight turned to snails—folk deemed omen of clan extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Rice turning to snails foretold clan wipeout.

sentences.zh: 有司簿閱崇水碓三餘區，蒼頭八百餘人，他珍寶貨賄田宅稱是。

translations.literal: Authorities inventoried Chong's water mills over thirty districts, household slaves over eight hundred; other treasures bribes fields houses matched.
translations.idiomatic: Auditors tallied mills, slaves, and estates.

sentences.zh: 及惠帝復阼，詔以卿禮葬之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui restored throne edict buried him with minister rites.
translations.idiomatic: Hui reburied him with honors.

sentences.zh: 封崇從孫演爲樂陵公。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Chong's grand-nephew Yan Duke of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: A collateral heir kept the Leling title.

sentences.zh: =苞曾孫 -{樸}-=

translations.literal: The manuscript line reads equals great-grandson of Bao named Pu equals.
translations.idiomatic: Heading for Pu, great-grandson of Shi Bao.

sentences.zh: 苞曾孫-{樸}-字玄真，爲人謹厚，無他材藝，沒-{於}-胡。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Pu courtesy Xuanzhen was cautious and honest without other talents and died under barbarian rule.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu vanished into Later Zhao chaos.

sentences.zh: 石勒以與-{樸}-同姓，俱出河北，引-{樸}-爲宗室，特加優寵，位至司徒。

translations.literal: Shi Le sharing surname and Hebei origin adopted Pu as clan kin with special favor; he reached Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le favored him as fake kinsman.

sentences.zh: =附：歐陽建=

translations.literal: The manuscript line reads equals appendix Ouyang Jian equals.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix heading for Ouyang Jian.

sentences.zh: 歐陽建字堅石，世爲冀方右族。

translations.literal: Ouyang Jian courtesy Jianshi—generations a leading clan of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Jian from Ji great house.

sentences.zh: 雅有理思，才藻美贍，擅名北州。

translations.literal: He possessed logical insight and brilliant literary talent; his fame dominated the north.
translations.idiomatic: His prose dominated Hebei.

sentences.zh: 時人爲之語曰：「渤海赫赫，歐陽堅石。

translations.literal: People rhymed: Bohai blazing—Ouyang Jianshi.
translations.idiomatic: A ditty hailed him.

sentences.zh: 」-{辟}-公府，曆山陽令、尚書郎、馮翊太守，甚得時譽。

translations.literal: Summoned to duke's office he served Magistrate of Shanyang, Gentleman of Masters of Writing, Administrator of Fengyi—great timely praise.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through county and ministry.

sentences.zh: 及遇禍，莫不悼惜之，年三十餘。

translations.literal: When disaster struck none failed to mourn him; he was over thirty.
translations.idiomatic: His death at thirty drew lament.

sentences.zh: 臨命作詩，文甚哀楚。

translations.literal: Facing execution he composed verse painfully mournful.
translations.idiomatic: Final poems were heartbreaking.

sentences.zh: =附：孫鑠=

translations.literal: The manuscript line reads equals appendix Sun Shuo equals.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix heading for Sun Shuo.

sentences.zh: 孫鑠字巨鄴，河內懷人也。

translations.literal: Sun Shuo courtesy Juye was a man of Huai in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shuo from Huai district.

sentences.zh: 少樂爲縣吏，太守呉奮轉以爲主簿。

translations.literal: In youth happy as county clerk; Administrator Wu Fen made him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fen promoted clerk to chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 鑠自微賤登綱紀，時僚大姓猶不與鑠同坐。

translations.literal: Though risen from low rank to clerk supervisor fellow officials from great clans still refused seat beside Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles shunned his bench.

sentences.zh: 奮大怒，遂薦鑠爲司隸都官從事。

translations.literal: Fen raged and recommended Shuo Capital Affairs Investigator.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fen forced him into metropolitan inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉劉訥甚知賞之。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Commandant Liu Ne greatly recognized and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ne championed him.

sentences.zh: 時奮又薦鑠-{於}-大司馬石苞，苞-{辟}-爲掾。

translations.literal: When Fen again recommended Shuo to Grand Marshal Shi Bao, Bao summoned him clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fen sent him to Shi Bao's staff.

sentences.zh: 鑠將應命，行達許昌，會台已密遣輕軍襲苞。

translations.literal: Shuo set out to answer; reaching Xuchang court had secretly dispatched light troops raiding Bao.
translations.idiomatic: En route he learned court struck Bao.

sentences.zh: -{於}-時汝陰王鎮許，鑠過謁之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Yinyin Sima Shen ruled Xu; Shuo visited him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shen held Xu.

sentences.zh: 王先識鑠，以鄕里之情私告鑠曰：「無與禍。

translations.literal: Prince knowing Shuo from earlier privately warned: Do not join calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Shen urged retreat.

sentences.zh: 」鑠即出，即馳詣壽春，爲苞畫計，苞賴而獲免。

translations.literal: Shuo departed at once, galloped to Shouchun, laid plans for Bao—Bao relied on him and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: His warning saved Bao at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書郎，在職駁議十有餘事，爲當時所稱。

translations.literal: Promoted Gentleman of Masters of Writing he refuted over ten matters in office praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: As ministry gentleman his critiques won fame.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰

translations.literal: Historian states.
translations.idiomatic: Historian's verdict.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：若夫經爲帝師，鄭-{沖}--{於}-焉無愧；

translations.literal: Historian states: As for serving as imperial tutor in the classics Zheng Chong therein had no shame;
translations.idiomatic: As classical mentor to the throne Zheng Chong stood entirely above reproach.

sentences.zh: 孝爲德本，王祥所以當仁；

translations.literal: Filial piety roots virtue—therefore Wang Xiang bore humaneness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang embodied filial virtue.

sentences.zh: 何曾善其親而及其親之黨者也。

translations.literal: He Zeng honored kin and extended grace to kin's kin.
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng cherished extended family.

sentences.zh: 夏禹恭儉，殷因損益。

translations.literal: Yu of Xia was reverent and frugal; Yin revised increase and decrease.
translations.idiomatic: Historian cited Xia-Yin sumptuary roots.

sentences.zh: 牲牢服用，各有品章，諸侯不恆牛，命士不恆豕。

translations.literal: Victims and garments each had graded rules; feudal lords did not routinely use oxen; commissioned gentlemen did not routinely use pigs.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient ritual graded sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 禦而驕奢，其關乎治政。

translations.literal: Yet arrogance and luxury hinge on governing.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagance shapes policy.

sentences.zh: 乘時立-{制}-，莫不由之。

translations.literal: Seizing the moment to establish regulations none escape this.
translations.idiomatic: Every age codifies restraint.

sentences.zh: 石崇學乃多聞，情乖寡悔，超四豪而取富，喻五侯而競爽。

translations.literal: Though Shi Chong learned widely his temperament courted regret; he surpassed the Four Heroes seeking wealth rivaled the Five Marquises in pride.
translations.idiomatic: Chong outspent legendary wastrels.

sentences.zh: 春畦靃靡，列-{於}-凝沍之晨；

translations.literal: Spring plots lush spread through freezing mornings;
translations.idiomatic: His gardens flourished even in frost.

sentences.zh: 錦障逶迤，亙以山川之外。

translations.literal: Brocade screens wound beyond mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Silk barriers stretched past horizons.

sentences.zh: 撞鐘舞女，流宕忘歸，至-{於}-金-{谷}-含悲，吹樓將墜，所謂高蟬處乎輕陰，不知螳蜋襲其-{後}-也。

translations.literal: Bell music and dancing girls led revelers forgetful of return—until Golden Valley held grief and flute towers nearly fell—what is called the high cicada resting in light shade unaware the mantis strikes behind.
translations.idiomatic: His revels invoked the mantis-and-cicada parable.

translations.literal: The line reads praise equals equals.
translations.idiomatic: Double equals mark preceding encomium.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：鄭-{沖}-含素，王祥遲暮。

translations.literal: Encomium states: Zheng Chong embraced simplicity; Wang Xiang matured late.
translations.idiomatic: Elegy opens on Chong and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 百行斯融，雙飛天路。

translations.literal: All hundred conducts harmonize; pair soar heaven's road.
translations.idiomatic: Their virtues paired ascent.

sentences.zh: 何石殊操，芳飪標奇。

translations.literal: He and Shi diverged in conduct yet shared famed kitchens.
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng and Shi clan contrasted yet linked by luxury.

sentences.zh: 帝風流靡，崇心載馳。

translations.literal: Imperial customs flowed dissipated; Chong's heart galloped apace.
translations.idiomatic: Court fashion ran decadent as Chong raced excess.

sentences.zh: 矜奢不極，寇害成貲。

translations.literal: Arrogant luxury without limit turned bandit harm into profit.
translations.idiomatic: Boundless pride fed catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 邦分身墜，樂往哀隨。

translations.literal: The domain split apart and bodies plunged down; pleasure departed and mourning followed.
translations.idiomatic: Their realm shattered and houses fell—every banquet ended in ruin.
